resources.label: Elevator Pitch Rubric
resources.description: Scoring rubric for elevator pitch and value proposition quality covering time-to-value, core message clarity, differentiation, call-to-action quality, and memorability

resources.label: Core Message Clarity
resources.description: Evaluates whether the pitch communicates a single, coherent message in plain language tailored to the audience. Cognitive load theory requires one core idea per elevator pitch; multiple ideas compete and all lose. Source: Best-Practice Elevator Pitches.md; Best-Practice Product Descriptions.md

resources.label: Call-to-Action Quality
resources.description: Evaluates whether the pitch closes with a clear, specific, low-friction next step appropriate to the pitch context. The CTA should feel logically implied by the pitch — earned, not bolted on. Nudge theory applies: present a choice architecture where the easy option is to agree to a follow-up. Source: Best-Practice Elevator Pitches.md; Research - Using SOAR Storytelling most effectively.md

resources.label: Differentiation
resources.description: Assesses whether the pitch clearly establishes what makes the offering distinct from alternatives. Generic pitches that apply equally to any competitor provide no reason to choose. Differentiation must be specific, benefit-tied, and credible. Source: Best-Practice Elevator Pitches.md; Best-Practice Product Descriptions.md

resources.label: Memorability
resources.description: Assesses whether the pitch uses language, structure, and story elements that make it stick after the conversation ends. Based on Heath & Heath (2007) SUCCESs framework: Simple, Unexpected, Concrete, Credible, Emotional, Stories. A pitch that is forgotten fails regardless of quality. Source: Best-Practice Elevator Pitches.md; Research - Using SOAR Storytelling most effectively.md

resources.label: Time to Value
resources.description: Measures how quickly the pitch communicates its core value proposition. The best pitches follow BLUF (Bottom Line Up Front): the listener should understand what the product does and why it matters within the first two sentences. Source: Best-Practice Elevator Pitches.md

resources.label: Chart Type Appropriateness
resources.description: Degree to which the selected chart type matches the analytical task (lookup, comparison, trend, composition, correlation, distribution). Based on Vessey's Cognitive Fit Theory: performance is maximised only when the visual representation aligns with the task the viewer must perform.

resources.label: Colour Accessibility
resources.description: Use of colorblind-safe palettes, adequate contrast ratios for chart elements per WCAG 2.1 AA, and avoidance of colour as the sole encoding channel. A material share of viewers have colour vision deficiency, its prevalence library knowledge; red-green combinations are the most common failure mode. Redundant encoding (colour + shape/pattern/label) is required for accessible charts.

resources.label: Data-Ink Ratio
resources.description: Proportion of visual ink actually encoding data versus total ink in the graphic; its target ratio is library knowledge. Chartjunk (3D effects, decorative fills, heavy gridlines, moiré patterns, redundant tick marks, background fills) is extraneous cognitive load and must be eliminated. Formula: Data-Ink / Total Ink used to print the graphic.

resources.label: Insight Communication
resources.description: Degree to which the chart's title and annotations communicate the key analytical conclusion rather than merely labelling the subject matter. A Topic Title ('Q4 Revenue') forces the viewer to analyse and conclude. An Action Caption ('Q4 Revenue Grew, Driven by the Premium Segment') transfers the conclusion instantly, reducing cognitive load and increasing decision-making speed. Annotation quality and key takeaway visibility are also assessed.

resources.label: Labelling Clarity
resources.description: Quality of axis labels, data labels, title informativeness, and absence of separate legends requiring lookup. Direct labelling eliminates the split-attention effect where the viewer must split gaze between a legend and the data series to decode colour mapping. Titles must state the analytical conclusion (action caption), not merely describe the subject.

resources.label: Bloom Level
resources.description: The Bloom's Revised Taxonomy (Anderson & Krathwohl 2001) cognitive level an activity targets, from Remember through Create; an activity may span several adjacent levels

resources.label: Analyze
resources.description: Breaking down and examining components

resources.label: Create
resources.description: Producing new or original work

resources.label: Evaluate
resources.description: Judging based on criteria

resources.label: Remember
resources.description: Recall of facts and concepts

resources.label: Understand
resources.description: Interpretation and explanation

resources.label: Cognitive Complexity
resources.description: The depth of mental processing an activity demands of the learner, banded from low (single-answer recall) through medium (interpretation, comparison, application) to high (multi-step reasoning, judgment, or creation)

resources.label: High
resources.description: Multi-step reasoning, judgment, or creation

resources.label: Low
resources.description: Single-answer recall; minimal processing

resources.label: Medium

resources.label: Argumentation

resources.label: Clarification

resources.label: Conceptual

resources.label: Generative

resources.label: Procedural

resources.label: Recall
resources.description: Can reproduce facts or steps

resources.label: Evaluation Dimension
resources.description: Criteria for assessing the quality of AI-generated output and the operational performance of the system that produces it

resources.label: Coherence
resources.description: The evaluation dimension measuring whether generated output holds together logically and reads as a connected whole — internal consistency and flow, independent of whether its claims are true.

resources.label: Completeness
resources.description: The evaluation dimension measuring whether generated output covers everything the task requires, leaving no required aspect of the query or source material unaddressed — the recall-side counterpart to relevance.

resources.label: Factual Accuracy
resources.description: The evaluation dimension measuring whether the claims in generated output are true and correctly grounded in the source or established knowledge, as distinct from how well-formed or on-topic the text is.

resources.label: Hallucination Rate
resources.description: The evaluation dimension measuring how often generated output contains fabricated content unsupported by the source or context — the unsupported-content counterpart of factual accuracy, scored as a rate rather than a correctness judgment.

resources.label: Latency
resources.description: Time the system takes to produce its output — an operational performance dimension of the producing system, not a property of the generated content

resources.label: Relevance
resources.description: The evaluation dimension measuring how directly the generated output addresses the given query or task, regardless of its accuracy or fluency.

resources.label: Style Alignment
resources.description: The evaluation dimension measuring how well generated output conforms to the intended voice, tone, and formatting conventions, as distinct from what it says.

resources.label: AI Method Type
resources.description: The fundamental approach to using AI for content generation

resources.label: Agentic
resources.description: The AI method in which the model plans multi-step work, invokes tools, and iterates toward a goal, rather than producing output in a single prompted pass.

resources.label: CAG
resources.description: The AI method that pre-loads the full knowledge base into the model's context window (cache/context-augmented generation), eliminating runtime retrieval — suited to small, stable corpora and low-latency or offline use where RAG's retrieval step is unnecessary.

resources.label: Fine Tuning
resources.description: The AI method that adapts a model's weights by training on domain-specific data for specialised behaviour — the only method type that modifies the model itself rather than its inputs or context.

resources.label: PDL Declarative
resources.description: The AI method that expresses prompt programs in IBM's Prompt Declaration Language, a declarative format that makes multi-step LLM pipelines structured and reproducible rather than hand-assembled per run.

resources.label: Prompt Engineering
resources.description: The AI method that guides model behaviour solely by crafting the input text, leaving model weights unmodified and drawing knowledge only from the prompt context rather than external retrieval or training data.

resources.label: RAG
resources.description: The AI method that augments generation by retrieving relevant content from an external knowledge store at query time, distinguishing it from siblings that rely only on the prompt, pre-loaded context, or model weights.

resources.label: Pipeline Stage
resources.description: The phase within an AI content generation pipeline

resources.label: Chunking
resources.description: The pipeline stage that splits ingested documents into retrieval-sized segments, choosing split strategy and overlap so each chunk stands alone as a unit of retrieval.

resources.label: Embedding
resources.description: The pipeline stage that converts text chunks into vector representations via an embedding model, producing the numeric form that indexing and dense retrieval operate on.

resources.label: Evaluation
resources.description: The pipeline stage that assesses generated output against quality criteria — via LLM judges, metric scorers, or human review — closing the loop on the pipeline.

resources.label: Generation
resources.description: The pipeline stage that produces the final output by applying the LLM to a prompt assembled from the task and any retrieved context.

resources.label: Indexing
resources.description: The pipeline stage that stores embeddings and their metadata in a searchable vector store, making the processed corpus queryable by the retrieval stage.

resources.label: Ingestion
resources.description: The pipeline stage that loads, parses, and preprocesses source documents, turning raw inputs into text and metadata the downstream stages can consume.

resources.label: Reranking
resources.description: Post-retrieval pipeline stage that reorders the candidate passages returned by a first-stage retriever so the most relevant context enters generation. A stage rather than a retrieval strategy — it presupposes dense, sparse, or hybrid first-stage retrieval and composes with all of them.

resources.label: Retrieval
resources.description: The pipeline stage that queries the index to find the chunks most relevant to a given input, supplying the context that generation will consume.

resources.label: Prompt Pattern
resources.description: The structural pattern used in prompt construction

resources.label: Chain Of Thought
resources.description: The prompt pattern that elicits explicit step-by-step reasoning before the final answer (chain-of-thought prompting, per Wei et al.), improving multi-step problem performance over direct answering.

resources.label: Decomposition
resources.description: The prompt pattern that breaks a complex task into sequential sub-tasks with intermediate outputs, each feeding the next, instead of prompting for the end result in a single pass.

resources.label: Few Shot
resources.description: The prompt pattern that includes a small set of input/output examples (typically 2-5) in the prompt to calibrate the model's behaviour before the actual task.

resources.label: ReAct
resources.description: The prompt pattern that interleaves reasoning traces with tool-using action steps (ReAct, per Yao et al.), letting each action's observation inform the next thought instead of separating reasoning from acting.

resources.label: Role Prompting
resources.description: The prompt pattern that assigns the model a persona or expert identity to shape the style, depth, and framing of its response, rather than altering the task instruction itself.

resources.label: Self Consistency
resources.description: The prompt pattern that samples multiple independent reasoning paths and selects the most common answer (self-consistency, per Wang et al.), trading additional inference for reliability over a single reasoning chain.

resources.label: Tree Of Thought
resources.description: The prompt pattern that explores multiple reasoning branches and selects the most promising path — generalising chain-of-thought's single linear trace into a search over a tree of intermediate thoughts (tree-of-thoughts, per Yao et al.).

resources.label: Zero Shot
resources.description: The prompt pattern that issues a direct instruction with no worked examples, relying entirely on the model's pretrained capability.

resources.label: Retrieval Strategy
resources.description: The approach used to find and surface relevant context

resources.label: Dense Retrieval
resources.description: The retrieval strategy that matches queries to passages by semantic similarity of embedding vectors, capturing paraphrase and meaning that keyword matching misses, at the cost of embedding-quality dependence and compute.

resources.label: Hybrid Retrieval
resources.description: The retrieval strategy that combines dense and sparse retrieval and fuses their results, balancing semantic recall against exact-term precision at the cost of tuning complexity.

resources.label: Multi Hop
resources.description: The retrieval strategy that retrieves iteratively, using each step's results to inform the next query, so evidence spread across multiple linked documents can be assembled progressively.

resources.label: Sparse Retrieval
resources.description: The retrieval strategy that matches on keyword statistics such as TF-IDF or BM25 — fast, interpretable, and faithful to exact terms, but blind to synonyms and vocabulary mismatch, in contrast to dense retrieval.

resources.label: Argumentation Framework
resources.description: Framework representing the anatomy, typing, deliberative mapping, formal evaluation, or computational extraction of arguments rather than general text coherence

resources.label: Argument Mining
resources.description: Computational extraction of argumentative components and support/attack relations from natural-language text, operationalising claim-premise, Toulmin, and scheme-based models (Stab & Gurevych 2017; Lawrence & Reed 2019)

resources.label: Dung Abstract Argumentation
resources.description: Formal evaluation of a supplied set of arguments and a binary attack relation, computing which argument sets are collectively acceptable under extension or labelling semantics; argument content is deliberately abstracted away (Dung 1995)

resources.label: Issue-Based Information System
resources.description: Deliberation grammar mapping wicked-problem discussion into issues, positions, and pro/con arguments under a deliberately constrained link grammar; records what was said, not what is valid (Kunz & Rittel 1970)

resources.label: Toulmin Model
resources.description: Layout of a single practical argument in six functional roles — claim, grounds, warrant, backing, qualifier, rebuttal — with field-invariant structure and field-dependent standards (Toulmin 1958)

resources.label: Walton Argumentation Schemes
resources.description: Stereotypical defeasible reasoning patterns, each paired with critical questions whose answers restore or defeat the presumption the scheme licenses (Walton, Reed & Macagno 2008)

resources.label: Communication Framework
resources.description: Prescriptive framework for producing well-structured communication, in contrast to the analytical frameworks that represent what an existing text or argument is

resources.label: Pyramid Principle
resources.description: Answer-first communication structure with vertical question-answer logic, MECE horizontal groupings, and SCQA introductions (Minto 1985)

resources.label: Discourse Structure Framework
resources.description: Framework representing how spans of a text or dialogue connect into discourse structure; members differ in structural commitment — a single complete tree, local relation pairs only, or a directed acyclic graph

resources.label: Enhanced Rhetorical Structure Theory
resources.description: Signalled graph generalisation of RST adding typed discourse signals and secondary edges beyond the single tree (Zeldes et al. 2025)

resources.label: Penn Discourse Treebank
resources.description: Shallow, lexically grounded annotation of local discourse relations between two arguments, explicit or implicit, with no commitment to global text structure (Prasad et al. 2008; Webber et al. 2019)

resources.label: Rhetorical Structure Theory
resources.description: Represents a coherent monologue text as a single projective tree of elementary discourse units joined by nucleus-satellite or multinuclear rhetorical relations defined by constraints and intended reader effect (Mann & Thompson 1988)

resources.label: Segmented Discourse Representation Theory
resources.description: Formal-semantic discourse theory representing text or multi-party dialogue as a directed acyclic graph permitting multiple parents and crossing edges, built for non-linear conversation (Asher & Lascarides 2003)

resources.label: Scheme Critical Question
resources.description: A scheme-specific challenge whose answer can sustain, qualify, or defeat the defeasible inference.

resources.label: Claimed Similarity Question
resources.description: Checks whether the asserted resemblance holds.

resources.label: Is there a stronger counteranalogy?
resources.description: Tests whether another relevant comparison supports a conflicting conclusion.

resources.label: Is there a relevant difference between the cases?
resources.description: Tests whether a material disanalogy defeats or narrows the proposed transfer.

resources.label: Are the cited similarities relevant to the conclusion?
resources.description: Tests whether the similarities support the transferred property rather than merely resembling the target superficially.

resources.label: Is the source case itself established?
resources.description: Tests the truth and scope of the case from which the conclusion is transferred.

resources.label: Causal Evidence Question
resources.description: Challenges the evidence supporting the causal generalisation.

resources.label: Causal Interference Question
resources.description: Checks factors counteracting the predicted effect.

resources.label: Causal Strength Question
resources.description: Challenges the causal generalisation's strength.

resources.label: Consequence Evidence Question
resources.description: Challenges evidence linking action and consequence.

resources.label: Consequence Likelihood Question
resources.description: Challenges the predicted consequence's likelihood.

resources.label: Opposite Consequences Question
resources.description: Checks consequences carrying opposing value.

resources.label: Example Instantiation Question
resources.description: Checks whether the example supports the generalisation.

resources.label: Generalisation Strength Question
resources.description: Challenges the generalisation's strength and applicability.

resources.label: Example Truth Question
resources.description: Checks the example's attributed properties.

resources.label: Example Typicality Question
resources.description: Checks representativeness within the generalisation's scope.

resources.label: What exactly did the source assert?
resources.description: Tests whether the argument preserves the source's actual proposition, scope, and qualification.

resources.label: Is the assertion consistent with other qualified opinion?
resources.description: Tests whether credible peers materially disagree and whether that disagreement changes the presumption.

resources.label: Is the assertion supported by evidence?
resources.description: Tests the data, method, or reasons behind the opinion rather than relying on status alone.

resources.label: How credible is the source as an expert?
resources.description: Tests the source's qualifications, experience, and standing for this subject.

resources.label: Is the assertion within the source's field?
resources.description: Tests whether the proposition actually falls inside the expertise established for the source.

resources.label: Is the source trustworthy in this instance?
resources.description: Tests bias, conflicts, incentives, and reporting conditions relevant to the assertion.

resources.label: Access to Knowledge
resources.description: Tests whether the informant can know the relevant facts.

resources.label: Assertion Verification
resources.description: Tests whether the informant actually made the attributed assertion.

resources.label: Informant Reliability
resources.description: Tests the informant's honesty and trustworthiness.

resources.label: Alternative Means Question
resources.description: Tests whether another means can realize the goal, before comparing which option is preferable.

resources.label: Is there a materially better alternative action?
resources.description: Tests whether another feasible action advances the goal with a more favourable trade-off.

resources.label: Do adverse consequences outweigh the expected benefit?
resources.description: Tests material side effects, risks, and conflicts with other goals before accepting the recommendation.

resources.label: Is the proposed action feasible?
resources.description: Tests whether the actor can perform the proposed action under the stated constraints.

resources.label: Will the action advance the goal?
resources.description: Tests the strength and scope of the means–goal connection rather than assuming it from sequence or plausibility.

resources.label: Is the goal legitimate and genuinely valued?
resources.description: Tests whether the stated goal is an appropriate objective for the actual decision and audience.

resources.label: Sign Correlation Strength Question
resources.description: Challenges the indicator's evidential strength.

resources.label: Classification Strength Question
resources.description: Challenges whether the classification premise is sufficiently strong or remains doubtful.

resources.label: Individual Property Question
resources.description: Challenges whether the entity has the property asserted in the individual premise.

resources.label: Scheme Premise Slot
resources.description: A named semantic role that an instantiated scheme must bind to actual argument components or support sets.

resources.label: Analogy Relevant-Similarity Premise
resources.description: States the similarities that are material to the transferred conclusion rather than merely superficial.

resources.label: Analogy Source-Case Premise
resources.description: States the cited case from which the proposed inference is transferred.

resources.label: Analogy Target-Case Premise
resources.description: States the case to which the proposed inference is applied.

resources.label: Causal Generalisation Premise
resources.description: States the defeasible cause-effect connection.

resources.label: Example Instance Premise
resources.description: Asserts the example's relevant properties.

resources.label: Expert Opinion Assertion Premise
resources.description: Records the exact proposition the qualified source asserts.

resources.label: Expert Opinion Expertise Premise
resources.description: Establishes the source's relevant expertise in the field to which the proposition belongs.

resources.label: Expert Opinion Field Premise
resources.description: Establishes that the asserted proposition falls within the source's relevant field.

resources.label: Popular Opinion Acceptance Premise
resources.description: Asserts widespread acceptance of the proposition.

resources.label: Position to Know Assertion
resources.description: Records what the informant asserts.

resources.label: Practical Reasoning Action Premise
resources.description: States the concrete action proposed as a means of advancing the goal.

resources.label: Practical Reasoning Goal Premise
resources.description: States the goal or audience-valued outcome the proposed action is intended to advance.

resources.label: Practical Reasoning Means–Goal Premise
resources.description: States the warranted connection by which the proposed action advances the declared goal.

resources.label: Sign Indicator Warrant
resources.description: Supplies the defeasible connection from indicator A to proposition B in the relevant kind of situation.

resources.label: Sign Observation Premise
resources.description: Asserts that the indicator A occurs in the situation under consideration.

resources.label: Slippery Slope Bad Outcome
resources.description: Identifies the unacceptable endpoint of the sequence.

resources.label: Slippery Slope First Step
resources.description: Identifies the initially proposed action.

resources.label: Slippery Slope Recursive Premise
resources.description: Claims successive plausible transitions from the initial step.

resources.label: Argumentation Scheme
resources.description: A defeasible inference pattern whose presumption is assessable only with its declared premise slots and critical questions.

resources.label: Ad Hominem Argument
resources.description: Challenges a person's argument through an adverse allegation about that person; the allegation's relevance must itself be justified.

resources.label: Argument from Analogy
resources.description: Transfers a defeasible conclusion from a cited source case to a target case on the basis of relevant similarities and after testing relevant differences.

resources.label: Argument from Cause to Effect
resources.description: Predicts an effect defeasibly from an asserted cause and a causal generalisation.

resources.label: Argument from Consequences
resources.description: Recommends or opposes an action by evaluating its anticipated consequences.

resources.label: Argument from Example
resources.description: Infers a generalisation defeasibly from a particular case or collection of cases.

resources.label: Argument from Expert Opinion
resources.description: Reasons defeasibly from a qualified source's assertion in its field to acceptance of the asserted proposition.

resources.label: Argument from Popular Opinion
resources.description: Invokes widespread acceptance as a defeasible reason to accept a proposition.

resources.label: Argument from Position to Know
resources.description: Accepts an assertion presumptively because its source has access to the relevant facts.

resources.label: Argument from Practical Reasoning
resources.description: Reasons from a desired goal and a feasible action that promotes it to a defeasible recommendation to perform that action.

resources.label: Argument from Sign
resources.description: Infers a state of affairs from an observed indicator associated with it.

resources.label: Slippery Slope Argument
resources.description: Opposes an initial step because a claimed sequence of transitions would lead to an unacceptable outcome.

resources.label: Argument from Verbal Classification
resources.description: Assigns an individual to a category through an attributed property and a classification rule.

resources.label: Scheme Variable
resources.description: A parameter of an inference pattern, distinct from a premise asserting a relationship among parameters.

resources.label: Analogy Transferred Proposition
resources.description: The proposition transferred between compared cases.

resources.label: Cause Variable
resources.description: The initiating event in the causal inference.

resources.label: Effect Variable
resources.description: The predicted event in the causal inference.

resources.label: Consequences Action Variable
resources.description: The proposed action assessed through its consequences.

resources.label: Expert Opinion Domain Variable
resources.description: The subject domain S to which the expertise and proposition are related; naming it does not establish the required field relationship.

resources.label: Expert Opinion Source Variable
resources.description: The source E whose expertise and assertion are at issue; identifying E alone does not establish expertise.

resources.label: Popular Opinion Proposition
resources.description: The proposition whose widespread acceptance supports a presumption.

resources.label: Position to Know Source
resources.description: The informant whose access to the facts is questioned.

resources.label: Sign Indicated Proposition Variable
resources.description: Proposition B whose truth is inferred from the observed sign, rather than independently assumed as a premise.

resources.label: Authenticity
resources.description: How closely the assessment mirrors real-world performance

resources.label: Abstract
resources.description: Assessment presented without real-world context — decontextualised items testing knowledge in isolation

resources.label: Authentic
resources.description: Assessment in which the learner performs the real task under genuine workplace conditions

resources.label: Contextualised
resources.description: Assessment framed within a realistic scenario, though the learner responds outside actual task conditions

resources.label: Simulated
resources.description: Assessment in which the learner performs the task within a safe replica of the real environment

resources.label: Cognitive Demand
resources.description: Bloom's level required to succeed at the assessment

resources.label: Analyze
resources.description: Succeeding requires breaking material into parts and determining how they relate to one another and to an overall structure

resources.label: Apply
resources.description: Succeeding requires carrying out a procedure or using knowledge in a given situation

resources.label: Create
resources.description: Succeeding requires assembling elements into a new, coherent, or original whole

resources.label: Evaluate
resources.description: Succeeding requires making judgements based on criteria and standards

resources.label: Remember
resources.description: Succeeding requires only retrieval or recognition of previously learned facts and terminology

resources.label: Understand
resources.description: Succeeding requires constructing meaning — interpreting, classifying, comparing, or explaining in one's own words

resources.label: Evaluation Purpose
resources.description: When and why the assessment is administered

resources.label: Diagnostic
resources.description: Pre-learning assessment administered before instruction to establish baseline knowledge and identify gaps

resources.label: Formative
resources.description: During-learning assessment that monitors progress and adjusts instruction while learning is underway (Kirkpatrick Level 2)

resources.label: Impact
resources.description: Organisational-level assessment measuring business outcomes and ROI (Kirkpatrick Level 4)

resources.label: Summative
resources.description: End-of-learning assessment evaluating overall achievement against objectives after instruction (Kirkpatrick Level 2)

resources.label: Transfer
resources.description: Post-learning assessment measuring on-the-job application of skills (Kirkpatrick Level 3)

resources.label: Feedback Mechanism
resources.description: How results are communicated back to the learner

resources.label: Automated Delayed
resources.description: System-generated feedback released after a delay, such as when an attempt window or cohort deadline closes

resources.label: Automated Immediate
resources.description: System-generated feedback delivered to the learner the moment a response is submitted

resources.label: Instructor Verbal
resources.description: Spoken feedback delivered by the instructor, live or recorded, rather than in writing

resources.label: Instructor Written
resources.description: Individual written commentary composed by the instructor and returned to the learner

resources.label: Peer Review
resources.description: Feedback provided by fellow learners reviewing one another's responses or work products

resources.label: Rubric Based
resources.description: Feedback structured against the explicit criteria and levels of a rubric rather than free-form commentary

resources.label: Self Reflection
resources.description: The learner generates their own feedback by reflecting on performance against objectives or criteria

resources.label: Item Format
resources.description: How the learner interacts with the assessment

resources.label: Constructed Response
resources.description: Learner generates an original answer such as a short answer, essay, or code submission; reaches up to Create

resources.label: Observational
resources.description: An assessor observes and rates learner behaviour in context, as in coaching observation or manager rating; cognitive ceiling around Evaluate

resources.label: Performance Based
resources.description: Learner demonstrates skill through authentic task execution such as simulation, roleplay, or product build; reaches up to Create

resources.label: Selected Response
resources.description: Learner selects from predetermined options such as multiple choice, matching, or ordering; cognitive ceiling around Understand

resources.label: Kirkpatrick Level
resources.description: Which level of the Kirkpatrick model the assessment targets

resources.label: Behaviour
resources.description: Kirkpatrick Level 3 — measures on-the-job application and behavioural change

resources.label: Learning
resources.description: Kirkpatrick Level 2 — measures knowledge acquisition, skill development, and attitude change

resources.label: Reaction
resources.description: Kirkpatrick Level 1 — measures learner satisfaction, engagement, and perceived relevance

resources.label: Results
resources.description: Kirkpatrick Level 4 — measures organisational impact, productivity gains, and business ROI

resources.label: Narrative Arc Type
resources.description: The trajectory of change the archetype undergoes or catalyses across the story

resources.label: Flat
resources.description: An arc in which the character remains essentially unchanged, instead catalysing change in others or the surrounding world — the steadfast arc of character-arc theory

resources.label: Negative Change
resources.description: An arc in which the character declines or is corrupted, ending worse off than they began — the tragic counterpart to the positive change arc (McKee 1997)

resources.label: Positive Change
resources.description: An arc in which the character grows toward a better state, ending the story stronger or better off than they began — the standard change arc of character-arc theory (McKee 1997)

resources.label: Archetype Function
resources.description: What the archetype does within the narrative

resources.label: Advocacy
resources.description: Actively champions the protagonist's cause within an organisation or buying committee, converting internal resistance and building momentum before the decision

resources.label: Disruption
resources.description: Introduces chaos, humour, or unexpected perspectives — the trickster function that breaks expectations at any phase

resources.label: Enablement
resources.description: Provides tools, knowledge, or support to make success possible — the function of mentors and guides during preparation and approach

resources.label: Initiation
resources.description: Triggers the narrative by disrupting the status quo — the function of herald figures at the inciting incident

resources.label: Opposition
resources.description: Creates conflict and raises stakes — the function of villain figures at complication and crisis

resources.label: Testing
resources.description: Validates readiness and commitment — the function of threshold guardians and evaluators at threshold crossings

resources.label: Transformation
resources.description: Drives change from one state to another — the function of hero figures at climax and resolution

resources.label: Validation
resources.description: Confirms the protagonist's solution or journey by demonstrating visible positive outcomes, building credibility through proof at resolution

resources.label: B2B Buying Role
resources.description: The purchasing-committee role the archetype occupies in enterprise sales narratives

resources.label: Approver
resources.description: The committee member holding final sign-off and budget authority, who must be persuaded before the purchase concludes

resources.label: Champion
resources.description: The internal advocate who actively promotes the solution inside the buying organisation, converting resistance and building momentum toward the decision

resources.label: Influencer
resources.description: A committee member who shapes the opinions of decision-makers without holding direct purchase authority

resources.label: Skeptic
resources.description: The committee member who doubts and challenges the vendor's claims, forcing stronger proof — a disruptor whose objections must be answered rather than avoided

resources.label: Technical Evaluator
resources.description: The committee member who tests the solution's technical fitness and compliance — a gatekeeper whose assessment must be passed before commitment

resources.label: User
resources.description: The stakeholder who will work with the solution day-to-day and judges it on practical usability rather than strategic or budgetary grounds

resources.label: Corporate Applicability
resources.description: How readily the archetype maps to business storytelling contexts

resources.label: High
resources.description: The archetype maps directly to standard corporate narrative patterns — case studies, sales narratives, keynote stories, and B2B proposals

resources.label: Low
resources.description: The archetype is primarily relevant to creative or literary narrative analysis, surfacing in business use only for advanced critique or positioning work

resources.label: Medium
resources.description: The archetype is useful in specific corporate contexts such as change-management, compliance, and stakeholder narratives rather than everyday business storytelling

resources.label: Narrative Role
resources.description: The functional role the archetype plays in the story structure

resources.label: Antagonist
resources.description: The force creating conflict, obstacles, or tension — the resistance that makes the hero's journey meaningful

resources.label: Catalyst
resources.description: The character or event that initiates the story and calls the hero to action, disrupting the status quo to create the inciting incident

resources.label: Disruptor
resources.description: A character who challenges assumptions and introduces unexpected change, preventing complacency and forcing creative problem-solving

resources.label: Evaluator
resources.description: A stakeholder who assesses the protagonist's solution or journey before committing — representing the rational and political dimensions of commitment in B2B purchase narratives

resources.label: Gatekeeper
resources.description: A test or barrier that must be overcome before progress can continue, testing readiness and raising stakes before the hero enters the next phase

resources.label: Guide
resources.description: The character who provides wisdom, tools, or support to the protagonist, transferring the knowledge or capability that enables the hero's success

resources.label: Protagonist
resources.description: The central character who drives the story forward through action and transformation, providing the audience's point of identification and emotional anchor

resources.label: Transformer
resources.description: A character who undergoes visible change as a result of the protagonist's journey, validating the narrative arc for the audience through observed transformation

resources.label: Narrative Valence
resources.description: Whether the archetype is constructive, destructive, or ambiguous

resources.label: Ambiguous
resources.description: The archetype's role shifts or is contextually dependent — it may help or hinder depending on circumstance

resources.label: Negative
resources.description: The archetype creates obstacles or opposition to the protagonist

resources.label: Neutral
resources.description: The archetype serves a structural function without inherent positive or negative charge

resources.label: Positive
resources.description: The archetype contributes constructively to the protagonist's success

resources.label: Origin Tradition
resources.description: The theoretical tradition the archetype derives from

resources.label: B2B Stakeholder
resources.description: Buying-committee roles in enterprise sales narratives, where each stakeholder requires a tailored narrative approach based on their motivations and decision authority

resources.label: Business Narrative
resources.description: Corporate storytelling adaptations that cast the customer as hero and the vendor as mentor, with industry forces, market signals, and regulators filling the remaining roles

resources.label: Hero's Journey
resources.description: Campbell's monomyth structure as adapted by Vogler into eight archetypal roles — hero, mentor, threshold guardian, herald, shapeshifter, villain, trickster, and ally

resources.label: Jungian
resources.description: Jung's collective-unconscious archetypes expressing universal patterns of human experience — self, shadow, anima/animus, persona, wise old man, great mother, child, and trickster

resources.label: Learning Narrative
resources.description: Narrative roles adapted for instructional and training contexts, where learners are heroes navigating skill gaps and educators serve as mentors

resources.label: Proppian
resources.description: Propp's seven dramatis personae character functions derived from Russian folktale analysis — villain, donor, helper, princess, dispatcher, hero, and false hero

resources.label: StoryBrand
resources.description: Miller's SB7 framework positioning the customer as hero, the brand as guide, and three-layer obstacles (external, internal, philosophical) as the villain — the brand wins by empathy and authority, not force

resources.label: Content Modality
resources.description: The type of content the cognitive load construct applies to

resources.label: Interactive Module
resources.description: Interactive eLearning content risking navigation confusion and interactivity overload; its interactions-per-screen cap is library knowledge

resources.label: Slide Presentation
resources.description: Slide-based content whose primary load risks are text overload, split attention, and redundancy; its word, bullet and data-series caps are library knowledge

resources.label: Video Content
resources.description: Video or animation content risking temporal misalignment and information dump; its segment length and on-screen text caps are library knowledge

resources.label: Written Document
resources.description: Written or eLearning document content risking walls of text and undefined jargon; its paragraph and section caps are library knowledge

resources.label: Design Strategy
resources.description: The instructional design strategy for managing cognitive load

resources.label: Adaptive Scaffolding
resources.description: Adjust instructional support to the learner's expertise level, fading support as competence grows — targets intrinsic load

resources.label: Progressive Disclosure
resources.description: Present only what is needed at each moment and reveal complexity gradually, via builds, layered diagrams, and drill-down — targets extraneous load

resources.label: Retrieval Practice
resources.description: Strengthen learning through active recall using low-stakes quizzing, spaced repetition, and interleaving — targets germane load

resources.label: Worked Examples
resources.description: Provide step-by-step solutions for learners to study before attempting problems, fading steps as competence grows — targets germane load

resources.label: Expertise Sensitivity
resources.description: How the strategy's effectiveness varies with learner expertise

resources.label: Expertise Reversal
resources.description: Strategies that help novices but hinder expert learners — reduce or eliminate for expert audiences

resources.label: Novice Beneficial
resources.description: Strategies that significantly help low-prior-knowledge learners — apply liberally for novice audiences

resources.label: Universally Beneficial
resources.description: Strategies that help all learners regardless of expertise — always apply

resources.label: Load Type
resources.description: The category of cognitive load according to Cognitive Load Theory

resources.label: Extraneous
resources.description: Unnecessary cognitive effort imposed by poor instructional design — split attention, redundancy, chartjunk, or unclear hierarchy — which can and should be minimised

resources.label: Germane
resources.description: Productive effort spent on schema construction and deep processing — to be maximised once extraneous load is reduced

resources.label: Intrinsic
resources.description: Inherent difficulty of the material itself, determined by element interactivity and prerequisite knowledge — cannot be eliminated, only managed

resources.label: Mayer Principle Category
resources.description: The functional category of Mayer's multimedia learning principle

resources.label: Foster Generative
resources.description: Mayer principles that encourage deep engagement and meaning-making — multimedia, personalisation, voice, and generative activity

resources.label: Manage Essential
resources.description: Mayer principles that help learners manage inherent content complexity — segmenting, pre-training, and modality

resources.label: Reduce Extraneous
resources.description: Mayer principles that eliminate unnecessary cognitive processing — coherence, signalling, redundancy, and spatial and temporal contiguity

resources.label: Artefact Type
resources.description: The kind of instructional design planning document

resources.label: Action Map
resources.description: Visual diagram connecting business goals to performer actions to practice activities, minimising unnecessary content (Cathy Moore framework)

resources.label: Content Map
resources.description: Tabular planning tool aligning each module's objectives, topics, activities, assessments, and outcomes in a single view

resources.label: Course Blueprint
resources.description: Strategic-fidelity curriculum outline mapping modules to learning outcomes, audience, duration, and delivery method

resources.label: Screenplan
resources.description: Screen-by-screen outline specifying purpose, content summary, media, and layout for each display state

resources.label: Wireframe
resources.description: Low-to-medium fidelity planning document outlining the structure and flow of a learning asset segment by segment

resources.label: Delivery Format
resources.description: How the content is delivered to learners

resources.label: Asynchronous
resources.description: Self-paced delivery that learners complete on their own schedule

resources.label: Blended
resources.description: Combination of synchronous and asynchronous elements in a structured learning journey

resources.label: Synchronous
resources.description: Real-time delivery requiring simultaneous participation of learners and facilitator

resources.label: Design Phase
resources.description: The stage in the instructional design workflow

resources.label: Design
resources.description: Detailed structural planning — wireframes, screenplans, and interaction design

resources.label: Development
resources.description: Content creation — storyboards, scripts, media production, and authoring

resources.label: Discovery
resources.description: Needs analysis, audience research, and business goal identification

resources.label: Evaluation
resources.description: Measuring effectiveness, gathering feedback, and planning reinforcement

resources.label: Planning
resources.description: Strategic design decisions — objectives, structure, assessment strategy, and content mapping

resources.label: Production
resources.description: Building the final learning asset — recording, animating, assembling, and publishing

resources.label: Pedagogical Function
resources.description: The instructional role the content plays within a learning sequence

resources.label: Assessment And Closure
resources.description: Stage 7 — summative evaluation and transition to next learning or application; its duration is library knowledge

resources.label: Core Instruction
resources.description: Stage 4 — primary content delivery: the main explanatory, demonstrative, or exploratory material; its segment duration is library knowledge

resources.label: Hook And Opening
resources.description: Stage 1 — attention-grabbing introduction that motivates learners and creates relevance; its duration is library knowledge

resources.label: Practice And Retrieval
resources.description: Stage 5 — in-line knowledge checks, activities, and retrieval practice embedded within or after core content; its check duration is library knowledge

resources.label: Pre Training
resources.description: Stage 3 — foundational vocabulary and prerequisite concepts taught before the main complexity; its duration is library knowledge

resources.label: Roadmap
resources.description: Stage 2 — advance organiser previewing what the learner will cover, establishing expectations and a mental framework; its duration is library knowledge

resources.label: Summary And Reflection
resources.description: Stage 6 — consolidation of key points and personal reflection on how to apply the learning; its duration is library knowledge

resources.label: Structural Granularity
resources.description: The hierarchical level of the content unit

resources.label: Course Level
resources.description: The entire learning programme or curriculum, spanning hours to days and containing modules

resources.label: Module Level
resources.description: A distinct unit of instruction organised around a cluster of related learning objectives; its duration band is library knowledge

resources.label: Scene Level
resources.description: A single view, shot, or screen state within a segment; its duration band is library knowledge

resources.label: Segment Level
resources.description: A self-contained portion of content, typically one pedagogical sequence stage; its duration band is library knowledge

resources.label: Topic Level
resources.description: A major subject area or concept group within a module; its duration band is library knowledge

resources.label: delivery_mode
resources.description: Primary delivery modality for the content format

resources.label: Blended
resources.description: Delivery combining live facilitated sessions with self-paced components in one structured journey

resources.label: eLearning
resources.description: Self-paced interactive digital delivery completed without a live facilitator

resources.label: ILT
resources.description: Instructor-led training delivered live and in person to a cohort

resources.label: On The Job
resources.description: Delivery embedded in real work, where learning happens while performing actual tasks, supported by coaching or performance support

resources.label: Self Directed
resources.description: Learner-controlled delivery in which the individual chooses what, when, and how to study, without an imposed pathway

resources.label: Virtual ILT
resources.description: Instructor-led training delivered live over video conferencing rather than in a physical room

resources.label: duration_band
resources.description: Content duration classification ordered from nano through extended; the band boundaries are library knowledge

resources.label: Extended
resources.description: The longest band — a full course, bootcamp, or multi-day programme

resources.label: Long
resources.description: The long band — a workshop or multi-module block

resources.label: Medium
resources.description: The medium band — a full learning module or coaching session

resources.label: Micro
resources.description: The microlearning band — a single-objective microlearning unit

resources.label: Nano
resources.description: The shortest band — a single fact or concept, such as a knowledge burst

resources.label: Short
resources.description: The short band — a focused topic treatment or practice drill

resources.label: format_type
resources.description: Primary content format category determining structural requirements and production approach

resources.label: Assessment
resources.description: Content that measures learner knowledge or performance against objectives rather than teaching new material

resources.label: Formal Learning
resources.description: Structured content with defined objectives, progression, and assessment — courses, modules, workshops, bootcamps, and webinars

resources.label: Job Aid
resources.description: Quick-reference support for a specific task or process, used at the moment of need rather than studied for learning

resources.label: Practice Activity
resources.description: Content whose primary purpose is skill rehearsal — structured drills, exercises, and scenarios in which the learner performs rather than consumes

resources.label: Reference Material
resources.description: Lookup content organised for consultation rather than sequential study — reference cards, glossaries, and terminology guides for on-demand fact retrieval

resources.label: action_title
resources.description: A declarative slide header asserting a claim of value (Minto).

resources.label: bloom_verb
resources.description: An observable-capability verb for learning objectives — _apply_, _evaluate_, _create_.

resources.label: check_for_understanding
resources.description: Formative assessment that surfaces misconceptions and triggers correction.

resources.label: commercial_ask
resources.description: A close that requests a resource commitment (budget, sign-off, next meeting).

resources.label: facilitator
resources.description: The instructor / coach delivering training.

resources.label: facilitator_critique
resources.description: A review checking scaffolding clarity and cognitive load.

resources.label: facilitator_guide
resources.description: Speaker notes giving step-by-step instructions, activity debriefs, and timing for training.

resources.label: gain_attention
resources.description: A training opening that activates prior knowledge and primes cognitive load (Gagné Event 1).

resources.label: hook
resources.description: A business opening that builds rhetorical tension (SCQA Situation, provocative claim).

resources.label: imperative_verb
resources.description: A commitment-requesting verb for business CTAs — _approve_, _invest_, _commit_.

resources.label: instructional_event
resources.description: A slide header naming a cognitive scaffold step (Gagné event, e.g. _Recall Prior Learning_).

resources.label: learner_resistance
resources.description: Cognitive barriers, prior misconceptions, or motivation gaps that impede learning.

resources.label: objection_handling
resources.description: Live response that defuses purchase risk.

resources.label: objections
resources.description: Financial, technical, or strategic barriers to buying.

resources.label: pacing_mode
resources.description: The pacing configuration (business: `one_shot_decision_moment`; training: `iterative_practice_loop`).

resources.label: presenter
resources.description: The persuader delivering a business deck — seller, executive, or subject expert.

resources.label: proof_point
resources.description: Business body content that proves the action-title claim (data, charts, evidence).

resources.label: red_team_critique
resources.description: A review simulating hostile or sceptical buyers checking for logical leaks.

resources.label: repetition_stance
resources.description: The repetition policy (business: `avoid`; training: `require`, spaced retrieval).

resources.label: scaffolding
resources.description: Training body content that facilitates cognitive processing (worked examples, practice items).

resources.label: scene
resources.description: The atomic visual unit of a `storyboard`. ONE narration slice + ONE cinematography decision + ONE frame image. **Distinct from `segment`**, which is the script-level narration unit in the upstream `video-script` wireframe — a `segment` may split into multiple `scenes` when visual flow demands a cut inside a narration block (but never inside the words; the script is inviolate). The cross-skill contract is `scene_index ≠ segment_index`; one or more scenes share an `upstream_segment_index` when split occurred. Bare.

resources.label: seller_notes
resources.description: Speaker notes giving delivery tips and objection handling for a business deck.

resources.label: transfer_plan
resources.description: A close that prompts the learner to integrate the skill into daily workflow.

resources.label: application_domain
resources.description: Downstream NLP task that consumes parsed discourse structures as input features.

resources.label: Abstractive Summarization
resources.description: Summarization that generates new phrasing rather than selecting source spans, using discourse structure to judge content salience (standard NLP task)

resources.label: Argument Mining
resources.description: Automatic extraction of claims, premises, and their support and attack relations, for which parsed discourse relations provide structural scaffolding (standard NLP task)

resources.label: Authorship Attribution
resources.description: Identifying a text's author from stylistic patterns, with habitual discourse-structuring choices serving as discriminating features (standard NLP task)

resources.label: Coherence Evaluation
resources.description: Scoring how well a text hangs together, using the parsed relation structure itself as the coherence signal (standard NLP task)

resources.label: Deception Detection
resources.description: Detecting deceptive text from linguistic cues, including atypical discourse structuring relative to truthful writing (standard NLP task)

resources.label: Extractive Summarization
resources.description: Summarization by selecting spans verbatim from the source, exploiting nuclearity-based deterministic tree pruning to decide which units survive

resources.label: Question Answering
resources.description: Answering natural-language questions over text, using discourse relations to locate the spans that bear the answer (standard NLP task)

resources.label: Sentiment Analysis
resources.description: Classification of evaluative polarity in text, with discourse structure enabling sentiment propagation through hierarchical weighting of spans

resources.label: discourse_framework
resources.description: Major computational discourse theories with distinct topological structures, scope, and recursion handling.

resources.label: eRST
resources.description: Enhanced RST augments a primary rhetorical tree with secondary relations and anchored discourse signals, allowing additional relations to be represented without replacing the primary tree.

resources.label: PDTB
resources.description: The Penn Discourse Treebank annotates argument pairs, relation types and senses for explicit and implicit discourse relations, without requiring a single document-wide discourse tree.

resources.label: RST
resources.description: Mann and Thompson's Rhetorical Structure Theory — highly recursive projective trees capturing global document structure, whose strict tree constraints force concurrent relations to be discarded

resources.label: SDRT
resources.description: Segmented Discourse Representation Theory represents discourse constituents and their semantic and pragmatic relations, including complex constituents and constraints on accessible attachment sites.

resources.label: nuclearity_configuration
resources.description: Structural configuration indicating relative semantic weight between spans. Determines which span carries the core communicative intent.

resources.label: Nucleus Nucleus
resources.description: Multinuclear configuration in which two or more spans carry equal semantic weight with no subordination (Mann & Thompson 1988)

resources.label: Nucleus Satellite
resources.description: Hypotactic configuration in which the nucleus precedes its supporting satellite, the nucleus carrying the core communicative intent (Mann & Thompson 1988)

resources.label: Satellite Nucleus
resources.description: Hypotactic configuration in which the satellite precedes the nucleus it supports, delaying the span that carries the core communicative intent (Mann & Thompson 1988)

resources.label: parsing_strategy
resources.description: Algorithmic approach for automated discourse tree construction from raw text.

resources.label: Bottom Up
resources.description: Shift-reduce approach that iteratively evaluates adjacent units in a working stack, building the tree from leaf EDUs upward — precise at intra-sentential boundaries but sequential, so early errors propagate

resources.label: Hybrid
resources.description: Ensemble approach using an efficient lower-parameter model for segmentation and a highly parameterised reasoning model for relation assignment, optimising both cost and accuracy

resources.label: Top Down
resources.description: Sequential-bisection approach treating the whole document as one macro-span and recursively predicting optimal split points — captures global coherence efficiently but loses precision at fine-grained boundaries

resources.label: relation_class
resources.description: RST-DT rhetorical groups and structural conventions; a coarse group does not fix semantic direction or nuclearity.

resources.label: Attribution
resources.description: RST-DT group for attribution and negative attribution; the satellite supplies the source of the nuclear content.

resources.label: Background
resources.description: RST-DT group for background and circumstance, supplying context for interpreting the nucleus.

resources.label: Cause
resources.description: RST-DT group for cause, result and consequence; direction depends on the fine label and nuclearity.

resources.label: Comparison
resources.description: RST-DT group for comparison, analogy, preference and proportion; members may be mononuclear or multinuclear.

resources.label: Condition
resources.description: RST-DT group for condition, hypothetical, contingency and otherwise, distinguishing unrealized conditions, hypothetical scenarios, recurrence and alternatives.

resources.label: Contrast
resources.description: RST-DT group containing multinuclear contrast and mononuclear concession and antithesis; group membership does not determine nuclearity.

resources.label: Elaboration
resources.description: RST-DT group for additional detail, general-specific, part-whole, process-step, object-attribute and set-member elaboration, example and definition.

resources.label: Enablement
resources.description: RST-DT group containing enablement and purpose, distinguishing facilitation of an unrealized situation from an intended goal.

resources.label: Evaluation
resources.description: RST-DT group for evaluation, interpretation, conclusion and comment; fine labels and nuclearity locate the assessment or concluding perspective.

resources.label: Explanation
resources.description: RST-DT group for evidence, explanation-argumentative and reason, distinguishing persuasion, factual explanation and an animate agent's reason for acting.

resources.label: Joint
resources.description: RST-DT group containing list and disjunction, joining nuclei through enumeration or alternatives.

resources.label: Manner Means
resources.description: RST-DT group containing manner and means, distinguishing the style of an action from the method used to accomplish a goal.

resources.label: Same Unit
resources.description: RST-DT structural pseudo-relation rejoining interrupted portions of an EDU; multinuclear by annotation convention.

resources.label: Summary
resources.description: RST-DT group containing summary and restatement. A summary may occupy nucleus or satellite; restatement reiterates nuclear content in a satellite.

resources.label: Temporal
resources.description: RST-DT group containing temporal-before, temporal-after, temporal-same-time, sequence and inverted-sequence; fine labels preserve chronology and nuclearity.

resources.label: Textual Organization
resources.description: RST-DT structural relation connecting schematically labelled text spans; multinuclear by annotation convention.

resources.label: Topic Change
resources.description: RST-DT group containing smooth topic drift and sharp topic shift; members may be mononuclear or multinuclear.

resources.label: Topic Comment
resources.description: RST-DT group containing problem-solution, question-answer, statement-response, topic-comment, comment-topic and rhetorical-question; fine labels distinguish roles and direction.

resources.label: schema_extraction_pattern
resources.description: Engineering pattern for representing and assembling discourse structures extracted from model outputs.

resources.label: Direct Recursive
resources.description: Represent nested tree nodes directly through recursive schema references; support and depth constraints depend on the selected output system.

resources.label: Flat Relational Adjacency
resources.description: Represent nodes and rhetorical edges as separate lists with explicit endpoint references, then reconstruct and validate the hierarchy locally.

resources.label: Progressive Chunking
resources.description: Parse local subtrees separately and link their roots in a later pass; cross-chunk relations and the assembled structure require validation.

resources.label: signal_typology
resources.description: Five distinct categories of discourse signals that indicate rhetorical relations, ranging from explicit lexical markers, a minority of relations, to implicit semantic, syntactic, morphological, and graphical cues that carry the majority.

resources.label: Discourse Marker
resources.description: Explicit lexical connectives that directly name a rhetorical relation — the most studied signal type, yet accounting for only a minority of discourse relations

resources.label: Graphical
resources.description: Signals derived from visual and typographic features of the text — punctuation boundaries, paragraph breaks, and section headings

resources.label: Morphological
resources.description: Signals derived from word-form variation, chiefly verb-tense shifts and person-marker changes between adjacent EDUs

resources.label: Semantic
resources.description: Signals derived from meaning-level relationships between lexical items across EDUs — lexical chains, synonymy, meronymy, and coreference; the largest signal category

resources.label: Syntactic
resources.description: Signals derived from grammatical constructions and clause-structure patterns such as parallelism, relative clauses, clause mood, and reported speech

resources.label: tree_topology
resources.description: The graph-theoretic structure used to represent discourse relations.

resources.label: Augmented Graph
resources.description: A primary tree augmented by secondary cross-branch edges that capture concurrent relations without abandoning the hierarchy — the topology of eRST

resources.label: Directed Acyclic Graph
resources.description: Graph structure permitting multi-parent dependencies and crossing edges while remaining acyclic — the topology of SDRT

resources.label: Flat Pairs
resources.description: Relations represented as argument pairs without imposing a single global tree; argument spans need not be adjacent.

resources.label: Projective Tree
resources.description: Strict single-parent tree with no crossing edges — the topology of classical RST

resources.label: Argument Component State
resources.description: Whether an argument component is asserted by the source itself or absent from it, so that unstated components are recorded as fact rather than authored

resources.label: Stated
resources.description: The source asserts the component in its own words

resources.label: Unstated
resources.description: The source does not assert the component; its absence is the recorded fact

resources.label: Argument Conflict Type
resources.description: How one position attacks another, using the ASPIC+ attack-type trio verbatim; typing a conflict never adjudicates it

resources.label: Rebuts
resources.description: Denies the other position's conclusion

resources.label: Undercuts
resources.description: Denies the inference connecting the other position's evidence to its conclusion

resources.label: Undermines
resources.description: Denies the evidence or premises the other position rests on

resources.label: Argument Link Type
resources.description: The typed connection between two claims in a macro-argument, profiled from argument mining's support and attack relations

resources.label: Addressed By
resources.description: The objection or caveat this claim carries is answered by the target

resources.label: Rebutted By
resources.description: The target claim attacks this claim

resources.label: Supports
resources.description: This claim gives support to the target claim

resources.label: Argument Role
resources.description: The functional role a component plays in one argument, using Toulmin's (1958) complete six-element layout verbatim — claim, grounds, warrant, backing, qualifier, rebuttal. The set is closed; membership grows only by registered amendment

resources.label: Backing
resources.description: The field-specific support for the warrant itself — the body of fact, statute, experience, or theory on which the warrant rests

resources.label: Claim
resources.description: The assertion or conclusion the argument establishes

resources.label: Grounds
resources.description: The facts, evidence, or reasons offered in support of the claim

resources.label: Qualifier
resources.description: The modal force with which the claim is advanced

resources.label: Rebuttal
resources.description: The condition of exception under which the claim does not hold

resources.label: Warrant
resources.description: The general licence connecting the grounds to the claim

resources.label: Discourse Relation Explicitness
resources.description: Whether a typed discourse relation is overtly signalled in the source or inferred by the reader, following the PDTB explicit and implicit method in which an implied relation records the connective that would make it explicit

resources.label: Explicit
resources.description: The relation is overtly signalled by connective or construction text quotable from the source

resources.label: Implied
resources.description: The relation is unsignalled and inferred; the single inserted connective sentence that would make it explicit is recorded as its basis

resources.label: Discourse Relation Sense
resources.description: The typed sense of a discourse relation between two stated spans of source content, profiled from the PDTB 3.0 sense hierarchy at Level-2 granularity

resources.label: Cause
resources.description: One span gives the reason for, or the result of, the other

resources.label: Concession
resources.description: One span creates an expectation the other denies while both stand

resources.label: Condition
resources.description: One span holds only under the circumstance the other states

resources.label: Contrast
resources.description: The spans are set against each other on a shared dimension of difference

resources.label: Instantiation
resources.description: One span gives a specific instance of the generalisation the other states

resources.label: Discourse Role
resources.description: The structural standing of one content unit relative to a stated purpose, decided by the deletion test from rhetorical structure theory's nuclearity

resources.label: Background
resources.description: Context that orients without carrying the purpose's substance

resources.label: Nucleus
resources.description: Central to the purpose; what is kept when one unit must be deleted

resources.label: Supportive
resources.description: Ancillary material serving a nucleus with evidence, elaboration, or explanation

resources.label: Analysis Granularity
resources.description: The level at which discourse analysis is conducted

resources.label: Clause Level
resources.description: Analysis conducted over individual clauses — the finest granularity, corresponding to elementary discourse units (standard discourse-analysis unit)

resources.label: Document Level
resources.description: Analysis conducted over the document as a whole, addressing global structure and overall coherence (standard discourse-analysis unit)

resources.label: Paragraph Level
resources.description: Analysis conducted over paragraphs, capturing relations between grouped sentences (standard discourse-analysis unit)

resources.label: Section Level
resources.description: Analysis conducted over document sections, capturing macro-structural relations between major divisions (standard discourse-analysis unit)

resources.label: Sentence Level
resources.description: Analysis conducted over whole sentences rather than their constituent clauses (standard discourse-analysis unit)

resources.label: Coherence Level
resources.description: The scope of the coherence mechanism

resources.label: Global
resources.description: Macro-level coherence achieved through topic progression and rhetorical organisation — topic sentences, section headers, thesis-support structure, and narrative arc

resources.label: Local
resources.description: Sentence-to-sentence coherence achieved through coreference, lexical repetition, conjunction, and ellipsis

resources.label: Relational
resources.description: Coherence achieved by explicitly signalling how discourse units relate to each other — discourse connectives, RST relations, transition phrases, and metadiscourse markers

resources.label: Complexity Tier
resources.description: The structural complexity of the discourse unit

resources.label: Complex
resources.description: A main clause with one or more subordinate clauses, introducing hierarchical embedding

resources.label: Compound
resources.description: Two or more independent clauses joined by coordination, with at most one level of embedding

resources.label: Compound Complex
resources.description: Multiple independent clauses combined with embedded subordination

resources.label: Multi Level
resources.description: Deeply nested discourse with four or more levels of embedding — the highest structural complexity tier

resources.label: Simple
resources.description: A single clause or sentence carrying one proposition, with no embedding

resources.label: Connective Function
resources.description: The semantic role of the discourse connective

resources.label: Additive
resources.description: Adds information without contrast or causality (and, also, furthermore, moreover)

resources.label: Adversative
resources.description: Signals contrast, concession, or an unexpected outcome (but, however, although, nevertheless)

resources.label: Causal
resources.description: Signals cause-effect, reason, or purpose (because, therefore, consequently, as a result)

resources.label: Conditional
resources.description: Signals contingency or hypothetical relationships (if, unless, provided that, assuming)

resources.label: Exemplifying
resources.description: Introduces examples or illustrations (for example, for instance, such as, namely)

resources.label: Reformulating
resources.description: Restates or clarifies previous content (in other words, that is, put simply)

resources.label: Temporal
resources.description: Signals time relationships or sequence (then, next, before, after, meanwhile)

resources.label: Discourse Relation Type
resources.description: The RST or discourse relation connecting two text spans

resources.label: Presentational
resources.description: Relations that work on the reader's inclination to accept a claim — motivation, antithesis, background, enablement, justification, and concession

resources.label: Subject Matter
resources.description: Relations holding between the semantic content of the discourse units themselves — elaboration, cause, condition, contrast, sequence, restatement, evaluation, and solutionhood

resources.label: Acceptable Argument
resources.description: An argument whose every attacker is attacked by the evaluating set.

resources.label: Admissible Set
resources.description: A conflict-free set defending all its members.

resources.label: Argument
resources.description: An abstract item whose internal reasoning is left unspecified.

resources.label: Attack
resources.description: A directed challenge from one argument to another.

resources.label: Characteristic Function
resources.description: Maps an argument set to all arguments acceptable relative to it.

resources.label: Complete Extension
resources.description: An admissible set containing every argument it defends.

resources.label: Conflict-free Set
resources.description: An argument set containing no internal attack.

resources.label: Grounded Extension
resources.description: The least fixed point of the characteristic function.

resources.label: Preferred Extension
resources.description: An admissible set maximal under set inclusion.

resources.label: Stable Extension
resources.description: A conflict-free set attacking every argument outside itself.

resources.label: Argument Direction
resources.description: Whether the evidence supports or challenges the claim

resources.label: Contextualising
resources.description: The evidence situates the claim in its background without directly strengthening or challenging it

resources.label: Opposing
resources.description: The evidence challenges or contradicts the claim

resources.label: Qualifying
resources.description: The evidence limits the claim's scope or attaches conditions to it rather than supporting or opposing it outright

resources.label: Supporting
resources.description: The evidence strengthens the claim, increasing its acceptability

resources.label: Argument Stance
resources.description: The relational stance of one argument component toward another in the argument graph

resources.label: Attack
resources.description: The component directly challenges the truth or acceptability of the target component (standard attack relation in argumentation theory)

resources.label: Partial Attack
resources.description: The component challenges only part of the target — a sub-claim or its scope — while leaving the remainder standing (argument-mining stance category)

resources.label: Support
resources.description: The component strengthens the acceptability of the component it targets (standard support relation in argumentation theory and argument mining)

resources.label: Undercut
resources.description: The component attacks the inferential link between the target's data and claim rather than the claim itself — Pollock's undercutting defeater from argumentation theory

resources.label: Evidence Category
resources.description: The kind of support presented for a claim — one of the genuine evidence types, or the declared sentinel value rhetorical_device marking persuasive support that is not evidence proper
