resources.description: Nucleus solves satellite's problem.

resources.label: problem-solution-s
resources.description: Satellite solves nucleus's problem.

resources.label: proportion
resources.description: Nuclei express proportional tendencies.

resources.label: purpose
resources.description: Satellite is nucleus's intended goal.

resources.label: question-answer
resources.description: Spans express a question and answer.

resources.label: question-answer-n
resources.description: Nucleus answers satellite.

resources.label: question-answer-s
resources.description: Satellite answers nucleus.

resources.label: reason
resources.description: A span explains an animate agent's action.

resources.label: restatement
resources.description: Satellite reiterates nucleus without interpretation.

resources.label: result
resources.description: Satellite causes nucleus.

resources.label: rhetorical-question
resources.description: Satellite poses a rhetorical question about nucleus.

resources.label: same-unit
resources.description: Structural convention joining interrupted EDU fragments.

resources.label: sequence
resources.description: Nuclei occur chronologically.

resources.label: span
resources.description: Structural link carrying nuclear content upward.

resources.label: statement-response
resources.description: Spans express a statement and response.

resources.label: statement-response-n
resources.description: Nucleus responds to satellite.

resources.label: statement-response-s
resources.description: Satellite responds to nucleus.

resources.label: summary-n
resources.description: Nucleus condenses satellite.

resources.label: summary-s
resources.description: Satellite condenses nucleus.

resources.label: temporal-after
resources.description: Nucleus follows satellite temporally.

resources.label: temporal-before
resources.description: Nucleus precedes satellite temporally.

resources.label: temporal-same-time
resources.description: Spans overlap temporally.

resources.label: textualorganization
resources.description: Structural convention connecting schematically labelled spans.

resources.label: topic-comment
resources.description: Topic precedes a specific comment.

resources.label: topic-drift
resources.description: Topic changes smoothly with shared focus.

resources.label: topic-shift
resources.description: Topic changes sharply to different focus.

resources.label: Assessment Scope
resources.description: The scope at which evaluation is applied — a content granularity from single interaction to whole portfolio, or a cross-cutting scope such as workplace transfer or delivery modality

resources.label: Deck Level
resources.description: Holistic evaluation of an entire presentation or content asset

resources.label: Interaction Level
resources.description: Evaluation of a single atomic interaction or question — immediate response validation at the card or item level

resources.label: Microlearning Level
resources.description: Evaluation of a short microlearning sequence — embedded quick checks and micro-feedback loops; the span it covers is library knowledge

resources.label: Modality Level
resources.description: Evaluation applied across one delivery modality, comparing content within that channel rather than judging a single content unit

resources.label: Portfolio Level
resources.description: Evaluation aggregated across multiple content assets — consistency, brand alignment, and quality trend

resources.label: Section Level
resources.description: Evaluation of a group of slides or a content section for structure, narrative flow, and evidence quality

resources.label: Slide Level
resources.description: Evaluation of a single slide or content unit for qualities such as visual clarity and cognitive load

resources.label: Workplace Level
resources.description: Evaluation applied to on-the-job performance after learning — workplace transfer rather than a content unit

resources.label: Cognitive Level (Bloom's)
resources.description: The cognitive complexity tier of the learning objective or assessment item, aligned to Bloom's Revised Taxonomy (Anderson & Krathwohl 2001)

resources.label: Analyse
resources.description: Requires breaking material into parts and determining how they relate to structure and purpose

resources.label: Apply
resources.description: Requires carrying out or using a procedure in a given situation

resources.label: Create
resources.description: Requires assembling elements into a new, coherent, or original whole

resources.label: Evaluate
resources.description: Requires making judgements based on criteria and standards

resources.label: Remember
resources.description: Requires retrieval or recognition of knowledge from long-term memory

resources.label: Understand
resources.description: Requires constructing meaning — interpreting, classifying, comparing, or explaining

resources.label: Evaluative Function
resources.description: The purpose and audience of the evaluation

resources.label: Benchmarking
resources.description: Compares quality against standards, peers, or historical performance, yielding comparative scores and percentile positioning

resources.label: Diagnostic
resources.description: Identifies specific strengths, weaknesses, and prerequisite gaps before or at the start of learning, to target improvement

resources.label: Formative
resources.description: Provides in-progress feedback that guides iterative improvement during the creation or learning process

resources.label: Ipsative
resources.description: Evaluates performance against the learner's or creator's own previous results rather than an external standard, tracking personal growth over time

resources.label: Summative
resources.description: Provides a final quality judgement for a completed asset, read by stakeholders, reviewers, and quality assurance

resources.label: Transfer Evaluation
resources.description: Assesses application of learning in the workplace after the formal learning event, at Kirkpatrick L3-L4, at the booster intervals the library states

resources.label: Kirkpatrick Evaluation Level
resources.description: The level of the Kirkpatrick Four-Level Training Evaluation Model at which the assessment operates

resources.label: L1 Reaction
resources.description: Level 1 — measures learner satisfaction, engagement, and perceived relevance

resources.label: L2 Learning
resources.description: Level 2 — measures knowledge acquisition, skill development, and attitude change

resources.label: L3 Behaviour
resources.description: Level 3 — measures on-the-job application and behavioural change

resources.label: L4 Results
resources.description: Level 4 — measures organisational impact, productivity gains, and business ROI

resources.label: Quality Domain
resources.description: The broad area of quality the dimension belongs to

resources.label: Argument Quality
resources.description: Dimensions covering the strength and credibility of claims and evidence — evidence quality, logical coherence, and source credibility

resources.label: Communication Quality
resources.description: Dimensions covering how effectively content conveys its message — clarity, structure, engagement, and personalisation of tone

resources.label: Design Quality
resources.description: Dimensions covering visual presentation, aesthetic effectiveness, and cognitive readability — hierarchy, typography, colour contrast, imagery, and layout

resources.label: Inclusion Quality
resources.description: Dimensions covering accessibility, diversity, universal design, and cultural appropriateness for diverse audiences

resources.label: Learning Quality
resources.description: Dimensions covering cognitive load management, instructional effectiveness, multimedia principles, and transfer to real-world application

resources.label: Validity Integrity Quality
resources.description: Dimensions covering whether instruments measure what they claim to measure and whether scores are free from systematic bias or construct-irrelevant variance

resources.label: Rubric Type
resources.description: The structural approach used for scoring

resources.label: Analytic
resources.description: Scores each dimension separately with distinct criteria per level — detailed diagnostic feedback at the cost of time to apply

resources.label: Confidence Weighted
resources.description: Adjusts each response's score by the learner's expressed confidence — rewarding calibrated certainty and penalising overconfident guessing to incentivise epistemic accuracy

resources.label: Holistic
resources.description: Assigns a single overall score from a general impression across all dimensions — fast to apply but low in diagnostic value

resources.label: Single Point
resources.description: Defines only the proficient level, with feedback noting deviations above or below — encourages qualitative feedback but needs skilled assessors

resources.label: Weighted
resources.description: Analytic rubric with different importance weights per dimension, reflecting strategic priorities in the composite score

resources.label: Score Tier
resources.description: The performance level assigned to evaluated content

resources.label: Developing
resources.description: Approaching expectations — shows promise but needs refinement; its score band is library knowledge

resources.label: Exemplary
resources.description: Exceeds expectations and models best practice; its score band is library knowledge

resources.label: Needs Improvement
resources.description: Below expectations — fundamental issues to address; its score band is library knowledge

resources.label: Proficient
resources.description: Meets expectations — solid and effective; its score band is library knowledge

resources.label: Alternation
resources.description: Presents disjunctive alternatives without asserting either constituent.

resources.label: Attribution
resources.description: Relates an agent to attributed content without committing to the content's truth.

resources.label: Background
resources.description: Supplies contextual information about an event or object; event-state background overlaps temporally.

resources.label: Complex Discourse Unit
resources.description: A group of discourse constituents interpreted together as a discourse unit.

resources.label: Commentary
resources.description: Adds an evaluation or opinion about the first constituent.

resources.label: Consequence
resources.description: Relates conditional antecedent to consequent without asserting either constituent.

resources.label: Continuation
resources.description: Adds a contribution at the same discourse level under a shared topic.

resources.label: Contrast
resources.description: Juxtaposes comparable constituents through opposition or denial of an expected consequence.

resources.label: Coordinating Relation
resources.description: Connects constituents at the same level of discourse structure.

resources.label: Elementary Discourse Unit
resources.description: An elementary segment contributing a discourse representation.

resources.label: Elaboration
resources.description: Develops a constituent through more specific information about its content.

resources.label: Explanation
resources.description: Provides an explanatory cause for the preceding constituent's situation.

resources.label: Narration
resources.description: Relates successive events belonging to a coherent narrative sequence.

resources.label: Parallel
resources.description: Relates constituents through corresponding semantic structure.

resources.label: Precondition
resources.description: Presents an event preceding the first constituent; this is reverse narration, not a logical conditional.

resources.label: Result
resources.description: Presents a consequence of the preceding constituent's situation.

resources.label: Right Frontier Constraint
resources.description: Restricts incremental attachment to the latest constituent and its available structural superordinates.

resources.label: Source
resources.description: Relates communicated content to its source; both constituents are treated as veridical.

resources.label: Subordinating Relation
resources.description: Connects a constituent to one elaborating or explaining it at a subordinate level.

resources.label: Certainty Direction
resources.description: Whether the marker increases, decreases, or does not affect perceived certainty

resources.label: Decreases
resources.description: The marker lowers the perceived certainty of the proposition — the direction of hedge markers

resources.label: Increases
resources.description: The marker raises the perceived certainty of the proposition — the direction of boost markers

resources.label: Neutral
resources.description: The marker leaves perceived certainty unchanged, expressing attitude rather than confidence — the direction of position markers

resources.label: Discourse Role
resources.description: The function the stance marker performs within the discourse structure

resources.label: Attribution
resources.description: Identifies the source or basis of a claim for credibility and transparency (according to, as X states, studies show)

resources.label: Boosting
resources.description: Strengthens the speaker's commitment and persuasive force — assertiveness and confidence projection in pitches, leadership, and advocacy

resources.label: Discounting
resources.description: Acknowledges a counterpoint or concession before reasserting the main claim with greater force — the concession-then-assertion pattern that pre-empts objections while the post-marker assertion carries the speaker's actual stance

resources.label: Evaluation
resources.description: Signals the speaker's judgement about propositions or events — opinion formation, critique, and commentary

resources.label: Hedging
resources.description: Protects the speaker from full commitment to a proposition — face-saving, academic caution, and diplomatic or risk communication

resources.label: Marker Type
resources.description: The primary category of stance marker

resources.label: Boost
resources.description: A marker that increases the certainty or force of a claim — strong modals, certainty adverbs, emphatics, and universal quantifiers (must, definitely, always)

resources.label: Hedge
resources.description: A marker that reduces the certainty or force of a claim — modal verbs, epistemic adverbs, perception verbs, and approximators (might, possibly, seems to)

resources.label: Position
resources.description: A marker expressing the author's evaluative attitude toward the proposition rather than shifting its certainty (fortunately, notably, so-called)

resources.label: Modality Category
resources.description: The type of modality the marker expresses

resources.label: Deontic
resources.description: Modality of obligation, permission, and necessity — what the speaker holds should happen (must, should, ought to)

resources.label: Dynamic
resources.description: Modality of ability, willingness, and disposition — the subject's capacity or inclination (can, able to, tends to)

resources.label: Epistemic
resources.description: Modality of knowledge and belief — how certain the speaker is about the truth of the proposition (might, probably, certainly)

resources.label: Evidential
resources.description: Modality of information source — the basis on which the claim rests, whether inference, hearsay, direct perception, or published record (reportedly, according to, research shows)

resources.label: Stance Polarity
resources.description: Whether the author supports, contests, or remains neutral on the proposition

resources.label: Contest
resources.description: The author signals disagreement with or opposition to the proposition (dispute, reject, challenge), whether evidence-grounded, corrective, or adversarial

resources.label: Neutral
resources.description: The author takes no clear evaluative position, reporting or describing without claiming a stake in the outcome (observe, note, report)

resources.label: Support
resources.description: The author signals agreement with or endorsement of the proposition (agree, endorse, advocate), whether on evidential, preferential, or deferential grounds

resources.label: Strength Tier
resources.description: The degree of impact the marker has on perceived certainty

resources.label: Moderate
resources.description: Noticeable impact on perceived certainty — possibly, perhaps, and suggests as hedges; clearly and obviously as boosts

resources.label: Strong
resources.description: Substantial impact on perceived certainty — might, could, and seems as hedges; definitely, must, always, and never as boosts

resources.label: Weak
resources.description: Minimal impact on perceived certainty — approximators such as somewhat and fairly as hedges, likely and probably as boosts

resources.label: Content Structure
resources.description: The organisational pattern of the written content

resources.label: Comparative
resources.description: Side-by-side analysis of options or approaches; suits product comparisons, framework evaluations, and decision guides.

resources.label: Definition Then Benefit
resources.description: Opens with a precise factual definition of the product or concept, then translates each feature into a concrete audience benefit; avoids opening with marketing claims. Suits product descriptions and knowledge-base entries.

resources.label: Hierarchical
resources.description: Top-down organisation moving from general to specific; suits executive summaries, course syllabi, and documentation.

resources.label: Inverted Pyramid
resources.description: Leads with the most important information and lets supporting detail follow in descending significance; the journalistic pattern suited to news articles, executive briefs, and abstracts.

resources.label: Linear
resources.description: Sequential progression from start to finish; suits tutorials, procedures, and narratives.

resources.label: Modular
resources.description: Self-contained sections that can be consumed in any order; suits reference guides, knowledge bases, and FAQs.

resources.label: Problem Solution
resources.description: Establishes a challenge before presenting its resolution; suits case studies, sales content, and thought leadership.

resources.label: Editorial Quality
resources.description: Key quality dimensions evaluated in editorial review

resources.label: Accessibility
resources.description: Usability of the content by readers with disabilities and by assistive technology — navigable structure, meaningful headings, alt text — measured against WCAG 2.1 AA practice.

resources.label: Accuracy
resources.description: Factual and technical correctness: claims, figures, names, and procedures verified against their sources.

resources.label: Benefit Clarity
resources.description: How plainly features are translated into concrete audience benefits, so the reader sees what they gain rather than what the product does.

resources.label: Clarity
resources.description: The degree to which meaning is grasped on first reading: unambiguous wording, concrete referents, and one idea per sentence.

resources.label: Concision
resources.description: Economy of expression: every word earns its place, with redundancy, filler, and throat-clearing removed without loss of meaning.

resources.label: Consistency
resources.description: Uniform terminology, style, formatting, and voice across a piece and its sibling artifacts, so the same thing is always named the same way.

resources.label: Diagnostic Precision
resources.description: In assessment writing, how sharply an item isolates the specific knowledge or misconception it is meant to test, so a wrong answer reveals why the learner erred.

resources.label: Distractor Plausibility
resources.description: In assessment writing, how credibly the incorrect options reflect real misconceptions, so items discriminate understanding rather than test-taking skill.

resources.label: Feedback Quality
resources.description: In assessment writing, how well formative feedback explains why a response is right or wrong and directs the learner's next step, beyond a bare correct/incorrect verdict.

resources.label: Inclusivity
resources.description: Use of bias-free, culturally aware language that excludes no reader and lets every member of the audience see themselves addressed.

resources.label: Memorability
resources.description: The likelihood that key messages are retained after reading, aided by vivid phrasing, strong structure, and deliberate repetition of core ideas.

resources.label: Specificity
resources.description: Preference for precise, concrete detail — named mechanisms, numbers, examples — over vague buzzwords and generic marketing claims.

resources.label: Tone Alignment
resources.description: Fit between the writing's actual voice and the tone register specified for the piece and its audience.

resources.label: Readability Target
resources.description: The target reading level for the audience

resources.label: Grade 6-8
resources.description: Plain-language band: short sentences and common words for broad general audiences and must-read operational content.

resources.label: Grade 9-12
resources.description: High-school band: standard business prose for general professional audiences, admitting moderate sentence complexity and everyday business vocabulary.

resources.label: Graduate Professional
resources.description: Advanced band: dense, abstraction-heavy prose for expert professional readers, as in white papers and scholarly analysis.

resources.label: Technical Specialist
resources.description: Level defined by domain expertise rather than a grade band: unglossed specialist terminology for practitioners in the field, as in API references and technical specifications.

resources.label: Undergraduate
resources.description: College-level band: sustained argument and discipline-general terminology for educated readers outside the specialism.

resources.label: Tone Register
resources.description: The voice and formality level of the writing

resources.label: Conversational
resources.description: Warm, relatable voice using contractions and direct address; suited to eLearning and video, avoiding passive voice, abstract nouns, and bureaucratic language.

resources.label: Empathetic
resources.description: Supportive, understanding voice that acknowledges challenges; suited to change management and onboarding, never dismissive, trivialising, or jargon-laden.

resources.label: Formal
resources.description: Professional, objective, impersonal voice that avoids contractions, colloquialisms, and first person; suited to executive audiences and regulatory content.

resources.label: Inspirational
resources.description: Motivating, visionary, aspirational voice; suited to keynotes and change communication, avoiding negativity, hedging, and bureaucratic framing.

resources.label: Professional
resources.description: Clear, direct, authoritative but approachable voice — the default register for corporate learning; avoids slang, hedging, superlatives, and marketing framing without specifics.

resources.label: Writing Mode
resources.description: The primary purpose and context of the writing

resources.label: Assessment
resources.description: Content designed to evaluate knowledge, understanding, or skill; produces quiz and multiple-choice items, scenario and reflection prompts, rubric descriptors, and formative feedback text.

resources.label: Copywriting
resources.description: Persuasive content designed to drive action or conversion, including product-focused writing that translates features into benefits in precise, specific language rather than generic marketing claims.

resources.label: Editorial
resources.description: Content expressing a perspective, analysis, or informed opinion rather than instruction or specification; produces thought-leadership articles, executive summaries, white papers, blog posts, and newsletters.

resources.label: Instructional
resources.description: Content whose primary purpose is to teach, explain, or guide a learner through a process; produces course modules, learning guides, how-to and knowledge-base articles, and practice prompts.

resources.label: Scriptwriting
resources.description: Content written for spoken delivery or multimedia production, where the words are heard rather than read; produces video narration, podcast scripts, speaker notes, and voiceover copy.

resources.label: Technical
resources.description: Precise documentation of systems, processes, or specifications, where accuracy and completeness outrank persuasion; produces API documentation, technical specs, release notes, and configuration guides.

resources.label: Abcd Method
resources.description: Framework for writing learning outcomes: Actor, Behaviour, Conditions, and Degree.

resources.label: Academic Bundle
resources.description: Formal 4-word phrase that creates distance between speaker and audience

resources.label: Accessibility Dimension
resources.description: Reference to accessibility, inclusion, or compliance as a quality dimension

resources.label: Accessibility Feature
resources.description: Accessibility-related visual elements

resources.label: Accessibility Violation
resources.description: WCAG violation accessibility barrier screen reader keyboard caption alt text contrast colour blindness

resources.label: Accessible Data Visualisation
resources.description: The architectural discipline of building non-visual access into data visualisations — dual visual and semantic structure, focus-driven audio description, live regions and sonification, designed in from the start.

resources.label: Acoustic Leadership Pillars
resources.description: Four core pillars of executive presence measurable through digital signal processing: Authority, Engagement, Clarity, and Empathy.

resources.label: Action Learning Project
resources.description: References to long-term project-based learning where teams tackle real-world problems with periodic live review sessions

resources.label: Action Title
resources.description: A slide or section header that states a conclusion or insight in a full declarative sentence rather than a topic label.

resources.label: Action Title Principle
resources.description: Consulting standard where slide titles are complete sentences articulating a specific insight or conclusion.

resources.label: Addie Iterative
resources.description: Iterative application of the ADDIE model within project management, featuring a central evaluation hub and continuous monitoring and control.

resources.label: A/B Testing
resources.description: The controlled-experiment method that splits traffic between two experience variants and measures which performs better against a defined goal metric before rolling the winner out; a core Adobe Target capability.

resources.label: Account Qualification Agent
resources.description: Sales-qualification agent delivered through Sales Qualifier, the add-on to Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition — it reads account signals to judge which accounts are ready for the next sales step and assists business development representatives with account research, outreach-email drafting, and CRM updates.

resources.label: Adobe Acrobat AI Assistant
resources.description: Acrobat's document AI — attributed, conversational answers over a single document or a PDF Space, with selectable personas and natural-language PDF actions.

resources.label: Adobe Acrobat (Desktop)
resources.description: The desktop surface of Acrobat — the installed application for PDF creation, editing, signing, and review on Windows and macOS.

resources.label: Acrobat Express
resources.description: The Adobe Express-powered creation surface within the Acrobat ecosystem — turning document content into designed, shareable graphics and social posts.

resources.label: Acrobat Generate Presentation
resources.description: Acrobat Studio's presentation-generation capability — producing a complete multi-slide presentation from a prompt and source documents, fitted to Adobe Express templates.

resources.label: Adobe Acrobat (Mobile)
resources.description: The mobile surface of Acrobat — reading, annotating, filling, and signing PDFs on phones and tablets.

resources.label: Acrobat PDF Spaces
resources.description: The Acrobat-branded surface of PDF Spaces — the same multi-document AI knowledge hubs addressed from within Acrobat.

resources.label: Adobe Acrobat Pro
resources.description: The full Acrobat edition — creating, editing, converting, protecting, signing, and exporting PDFs, with AI Assistant and e-sign features included.

resources.label: Adobe Acrobat Reader
resources.description: The free PDF viewer and annotator — reading, commenting, filling, and signing documents without paid Acrobat features.

resources.label: Adobe Acrobat Services
resources.description: The developer brand for Acrobat's cloud APIs — PDF Services, Sign, and embedding — for building document workflows into applications.

resources.label: Adobe Acrobat Sign
resources.description: Adobe's e-signature service — sending, signing, tracking, and managing legally binding agreements as a cloud workflow.

resources.label: Adobe Acrobat Standard
resources.description: The essentials Acrobat edition — creating, editing, converting, and signing PDFs without the Pro-only features.

resources.label: Adobe Acrobat Studio
resources.description: The next-generation Acrobat workspace uniting PDF productivity, AI Assistant insights, and Adobe Express creation — users build PDF Spaces from their documents and turn document insight into shareable content.

resources.label: Adobe Acrobat (Web)
resources.description: The browser surface of Acrobat — PDF viewing, editing, conversion, and signing at acrobat.adobe.com without an install.

resources.label: Adobe Advertising
resources.description: Adobe's advertising platform — cross-channel paid-media planning, buying, and optimisation spanning search, display, and connected TV.

resources.label: Adobe Advertising Cloud
resources.description: Former name of Adobe's demand-side advertising platform for planning, buying, and optimising paid media across search, display, and connected TV — continued as Adobe Advertising.

resources.label: Adobe After Effects
resources.description: The motion graphics, compositing, and visual-effects application — animated titles, effects, and composited scenes for video.

resources.label: Adobe Experience Platform Agent Orchestrator
resources.description: Central orchestrator for enterprise AI agents on Adobe Experience Platform.

resources.label: AI Assistant
resources.description: The conversational assistant embedded across Experience Platform applications — Experience Platform, Real-Time CDP, Journey Optimizer, Customer Journey Analytics, and Experience Manager — answering product and operational questions in natural language and hosting the purpose-built agents.

resources.label: Adobe Analytics
resources.description: Adobe's web and app analytics solution — collection, segmentation, and reporting of digital behaviour such as traffic, conversion, and pathing, with Analysis Workspace as its analysis surface.

resources.label: Adobe Animate
resources.description: The 2D animation and interactive content application (formerly Flash Professional) — frame-based animation for web, games, and broadcast.

resources.label: API-First
resources.description: The architecture principle of exposing every capability through APIs before, or instead of, a bundled user interface, so services can be composed into custom stacks — the design stance of Adobe Experience Platform and of headless Experience Manager delivery.

resources.label: Attribution Modeling
resources.description: Assigning conversion credit across the marketing touchpoints that preceded an outcome — first-touch, last-touch, or multi-touch models — to reveal which activity actually drove results; served in Adobe's portfolio by Customer Journey Analytics, Marketo Measure, and Mix Modeler.

resources.label: Audience Agent
resources.description: Audience-management agent surfaced in AI Assistant within Real-Time CDP (B2C and B2B) and Adobe Journey Optimizer — it lets practitioners explore, understand, and manage audiences in natural language, surfacing audience inventory, detecting significant size changes and duplicates, and retrieving audience sizes to support targeting and buying-group creation.

resources.label: Audience AI
resources.description: The AI capability family for audiences on Adobe Experience Platform — conversational audience creation, size estimation, fluctuation insight, significant-change monitoring, and growth forecasting, surfaced through AI Assistant and the Audience Agent.

resources.label: Adobe Audience Manager
resources.description: Adobe's data management platform (DMP) — building audience segments from anonymous and third-party data for advertising activation.

resources.label: Audience Segmentation
resources.description: Dividing a customer base into groups that share attributes or behaviours so each group can be targeted with relevant experiences; in Adobe Experience Platform, performed over Real-Time Customer Profile data.

resources.label: Audio Overview
resources.description: Acrobat's generative audio capability that turns a document into a narrated single-host audio overview, for listening instead of reading.

resources.label: Adobe Audition
resources.description: The audio recording, editing, mixing, and restoration application — waveform and multitrack workflows for podcast, video, and broadcast sound.

resources.label: Adobe Brand Concierge
resources.description: Adobe's agentic conversational-experience application — brand-governed conversations tailored to each visitor's intent, helping customers discover products, compare options, get instant answers, and receive guided recommendations in real time.

resources.label: Brand Experience Agent
resources.description: Experience-design agent available in Adobe Experience Manager — it helps teams design and orchestrate brand-consistent customer experiences across channels, proposing campaign ideas and recommending content and journeys that align with the brand's positioning end to end.

resources.label: Brand Governance Agent
resources.description: Governance agent available in Adobe Experience Manager Sites and Assets — it checks content, assets, and pages against brand rules (tone, claims, logo use, typography, imagery) and governance policies such as usage rights and expiry, flagging violations with remediation guidance.

resources.label: Adobe Bridge
resources.description: The desktop asset browser for organising, previewing, and batch-processing creative files across the Creative Cloud applications.

resources.label: Adobe Campaign
resources.description: Adobe's cross-channel campaign management solution for planning, executing, and measuring outbound campaigns — email at the core, with direct mail, SMS, and push.

resources.label: Campaign Management
resources.description: Planning, executing, and measuring outbound marketing campaigns across segments and channels — audience selection, scheduling, delivery, and response tracking; realised in Adobe's portfolio by Adobe Campaign and Marketo Engage.

resources.label: Adobe Capture
resources.description: The mobile application that turns photographs into reusable creative elements — colour themes, brushes, shapes, and patterns synced to Creative Cloud Libraries.

resources.label: CDN
resources.description: Initialism for Content Delivery Network — the geographically distributed edge-server network that caches and serves content close to users for speed and resilience; Experience Manager sites ship through a built-in CDN and the Experience Platform Edge Network follows the same distribution principle.

resources.label: CDP
resources.description: Initialism for Customer Data Platform — the system category that unifies customer data into persistent, activatable profiles; realised in Adobe's portfolio by Real-Time CDP.

resources.label: CEP
resources.description: Initialism for Customer Engagement Platform — the two-way customer-interaction system category realised in Adobe's portfolio by Adobe Journey Optimizer.

resources.label: Adobe Character Animator
resources.description: The performance-capture animation application — 2D puppets animated live from camera and microphone input, lip-sync included.

resources.label: Cloud-Native
resources.description: The architecture principle of building software as containerised, elastically scalable, continuously updated services designed for cloud operation rather than ported to it — the basis of Experience Manager as a Cloud Service and Adobe Experience Platform.

resources.label: Adobe Color
resources.description: The colour tool for creating, exploring, and saving palettes and themes usable across Creative Cloud applications.

resources.label: Adobe Commerce
resources.description: Adobe's commerce platform (formerly Magento) for building B2C and B2B storefronts — catalogue, checkout, and deep extensibility.

resources.label: Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service
resources.description: The fully managed, multi-tenant SaaS edition of Adobe Commerce (GA 2025) — Adobe owns hosting and continuous updates; composable and API-first, with the storefront built on Edge Delivery Services.

resources.label: Adobe Commerce Optimizer
resources.description: SaaS merchandising and optimisation offering in the Adobe Commerce family, built on Commerce microservices — AI-driven personalisation, testing, and real-time analytics layered onto a commerce backend.

resources.label: Content Advisor Agent
resources.description: Content-recommendation agent available in Adobe Experience Manager Assets and Dynamic Media — it finds and recommends existing content and assets that fit a brief, campaign, or audience, using metadata, tags, and performance data to propose on-brand, high-performing candidates rather than generating new content.

resources.label: Adobe Content Analytics
resources.description: The Experience Platform application (formerly Project Condor) that joins AI-derived attributes of content — people present, tones, keywords — with Customer Journey Analytics data to show which content drives engagement and revenue, and which characteristics explain why.

resources.label: Content Aware Fill
resources.description: Photoshop and After Effects feature that fills a removed region by synthesising from the surrounding pixels of the same image — a pre-generative technique that samples the image itself rather than a model.

resources.label: Content Fragments
resources.description: Structured, presentation-independent content in Experience Manager, authored against a content model and delivered through APIs (including GraphQL) to any channel — the unit of AEM headless content.

resources.label: Content Production Agent
resources.description: On-brand content generation agent surfaced within GenStudio for Performance Marketing — it takes teams from brief to content to activation through a conversational interface, covering campaign tactics ideation, ad and email generation, brand-object creation, and brand validation.

resources.label: Content Supply Chain
resources.description: End-to-end enterprise process model spanning Workflow & Planning, Creation & Production, Asset Management, Delivery & Activation, and Reporting & Insights.

resources.label: Creation & Production
resources.description: The Content Supply Chain phase in which creative assets are authored and produced at scale — served by the Creative Cloud applications, Adobe Express, and Firefly generative AI.

resources.label: Creative Cloud Libraries
resources.description: The shared-library service that syncs colours, character styles, logos, and components across Creative Cloud applications and teams so design elements stay consistent wherever they are used.

resources.label: CSC
resources.description: Initialism for the Content Supply Chain — Adobe's end-to-end process model for planning, producing, managing, activating, and measuring marketing content at enterprise scale.

resources.label: Customer Data Platform
resources.description: A system that unifies customer data from many sources into persistent, addressable individual profiles available for segmentation and activation; realised in Adobe's portfolio by Real-Time CDP.

resources.label: Customer Engagement Platform
resources.description: The system category for managing ongoing, two-way customer interactions across channels — messages, offers, and journeys responding to individual behaviour; realised in Adobe's portfolio by Adobe Journey Optimizer.

resources.label: Customer Experience
resources.description: The customer's cumulative perception of a brand, formed across every interaction from first touch to support — the outcome quantity the Experience Cloud portfolio exists to improve.

resources.label: Adobe Customer Journey Analytics
resources.description: Experience Platform's native cross-channel analytics application — joining online and offline event data into a single journey view queryable in Analysis Workspace, without the schema limits of traditional Analytics.

resources.label: Adobe Customer Journey Analytics B2B Edition
resources.description: The B2B edition of Customer Journey Analytics — account-level journey analysis that rolls person activity up to buying groups and accounts.

resources.label: Customer Journey Mapping
resources.description: Charting the end-to-end sequence of interactions a customer has with a brand across channels and time to expose gaps, friction, and the moments that decide the relationship.

resources.label: CX
resources.description: Initialism for Customer Experience — the cumulative perception of a brand a customer forms across every interaction.

resources.label: Customer Experience Orchestration (CXO)
resources.description: Adobe's enterprise portfolio framing (formerly Digital Experience/DX) covering Brand Visibility, Customer Engagement, and Content Supply Chain.

resources.label: DAM
resources.description: Initialism for Digital Asset Management — the system category for storing, governing, and distributing digital assets; realised in Adobe's portfolio by Experience Manager Assets.

resources.label: Data Collection
resources.description: Short name for Experience Platform Data Collection — the ingestion layer capturing event data through the SDKs, datastreams, and Tags into the Edge Network.

resources.label: Data Engineering Agent
resources.description: Data-management agent for Adobe Experience Platform — it accelerates the onboarding and ongoing management of data (schemas, mappings, and ingestion) so more downstream use cases can be supported without manual data engineering effort.

resources.label: Data Governance
resources.description: The Adobe Experience Platform framework of usage labels, policies, and enforcement that controls how customer data may be used — classifying sensitivity at field level and blocking activations that would violate policy.

resources.label: Data Insights Agent
resources.description: Analytics agent surfaced in AI Assistant inside Customer Journey Analytics Analysis Workspace — it answers plain-language questions about the data and automatically builds the appropriate visualisations and tables, grounded in the organisation's configured data views.

resources.label: Datastreams
resources.description: Server-side Edge Network configuration records that route collected event data to the configured services — Analytics, Target, Experience Platform, Journey Optimizer — and to event-forwarding destinations.

resources.label: Delivery & Activation
resources.description: The Content Supply Chain phase in which approved content is published and activated across channels and campaigns — served by Adobe Experience Manager and the Experience Cloud delivery applications.

resources.label: Adobe Developer Console
resources.description: The console where developers create projects, manage API credentials and OAuth flows, and administer integrations against Adobe APIs.

resources.label: Digital Asset Management
resources.description: The discipline and system category for storing, tagging, governing, and distributing digital assets at enterprise scale so approved assets are findable and reusable; realised in Adobe's portfolio by Experience Manager Assets.

resources.label: Digital Experience
resources.description: Adobe's business-category term for the Experience Cloud side of the company — the products and practices for delivering, personalising, and optimising customer-facing digital experiences, as distinct from creative production and document workflows.

resources.label: Adobe Dimension
resources.description: The 3D scene composition application for product mockups and brand visualisation — staging models, materials, and lighting without a full 3D pipeline.

resources.label: Adobe Document Cloud
resources.description: Adobe's document-productivity cloud — the umbrella spanning Acrobat, Acrobat Sign, Scan, and their shared cloud services.

resources.label: Adobe Dreamweaver
resources.description: The web design and development application combining visual authoring with a code editor for HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

resources.label: DXP
resources.description: Initialism for Digital Experience Platform — the industry category of integrated platforms for building, managing, personalising, and optimising digital experiences across channels; Adobe Experience Cloud is Adobe's DXP.

resources.label: Adobe Dynamic Chat
resources.description: Marketo Engage's conversational marketing application — AI-driven chat that replaces static forms with real-time visitor dialogues, qualifying leads, booking meetings, and syncing scores and routing back to Marketo.

resources.label: Edge Network
resources.description: Short name for the Experience Platform Edge Network — the low-latency, globally distributed collection and personalisation edge shared by the Experience Cloud applications.

resources.label: Event Forwarding
resources.description: The server-side counterpart to Tags — it sends event data collected through the Edge Network on to non-Adobe destinations for server-side processing and enrichment, without adding client-side weight.

resources.label: Adobe Exchange
resources.description: Adobe's marketplace for third-party apps, plugins, and integrations that extend Creative Cloud, Document Cloud, and Experience Cloud products.

resources.label: Experience Data Model
resources.description: Adobe's open standard framework for describing customer-experience data — schemas composed of classes and field groups that make data from different systems consistent so profiles, segmentation, and applications interoperate across Adobe and third-party systems.

resources.label: Experience Fragments
resources.description: Reusable groups of Experience Manager components with layout — a complete fragment of an experience that can be placed across pages and channels so the same composed content is maintained once.

resources.label: Adobe Experience Manager
resources.description: Adobe's enterprise content management platform, combining web content management (Sites) and digital asset management (Assets) to build, manage, and deliver web, mobile, and headless experiences.

resources.label: Adobe Experience Manager Assets
resources.description: Experience Manager's digital asset management application — storing, tagging, governing, and distributing approved assets at enterprise scale, with Dynamic Media renditions for channel-ready delivery.

resources.label: Adobe Experience Manager Edge Delivery Services
resources.description: Experience Manager's high-performance delivery architecture — document-based or code-based authoring compiled to pre-rendered pages served from the edge for maximum Core Web Vitals scores.

resources.label: Adobe Experience Manager Forms
resources.description: Experience Manager's application for digital enrolment — building adaptive forms and automated document communications connected to backend workflows and e-signature.

resources.label: Adobe Experience Manager Guides
resources.description: Experience Manager's structured-content application — a DITA-based component content management system for authoring, reviewing, and publishing technical documentation.

resources.label: Adobe Experience Manager Screens
resources.description: Experience Manager's application for digital signage — authoring and operating in-venue screen experiences from the same content platform as web channels.

resources.label: Adobe Experience Manager Sites
resources.description: Experience Manager's web content management application for authoring, managing, and delivering websites — including headless delivery and Edge Delivery Services for high-performance pages.

resources.label: Adobe Experience Manager Sites Optimizer
resources.description: The AI-first companion to Experience Manager Sites (incubated as Project Success Studio) that identifies improvement areas in page loading, component usage, and content delivery, and recommends concrete fixes across performance, accessibility, SEO, and engagement.

resources.label: Adobe Experience Platform
resources.description: The foundation layer of Experience Cloud — real-time customer data infrastructure (XDM schemas, Real-Time Customer Profile, segmentation, governance) on which the native applications Real-Time CDP, Journey Optimizer, and Customer Journey Analytics run.

resources.label: Adobe Experience Platform Data Collection
resources.description: The suite of Experience Platform technologies — Web and Mobile SDKs, datastreams, Tags, and event forwarding — for capturing customer-experience data client- and server-side and routing it to Adobe and non-Adobe destinations.

resources.label: Adobe Experience Platform Edge Network
resources.description: The globally distributed edge-server network that receives data from websites and apps through the Web and Mobile SDKs and returns segment qualifications and personalised offers within milliseconds; it serves all Experience Cloud solutions and hosts Tags and event forwarding at the edge.

resources.label: Experimentation Agent
resources.description: Experimentation agent surfaced in AI Assistant within Adobe Journey Optimizer Experimentation Accelerator — it centralises past and active experiments so teams can summarise tests, analyse results by audience, understand what worked, and get proposals for the next test with suggested KPIs and sample sizes.

resources.label: Adobe Express
resources.description: Adobe Express content-creation product used across creative-production and digital-experience contexts.

resources.label: Federated Search
resources.description: Experience Cloud's cross-solution search service — one permission-aware search surface over business objects (audiences, journeys, datasets, assets) across the Experience Platform applications, built on a unified search index.

resources.label: Adobe Firefly
resources.description: Adobe's generative AI family and creative studio — commercially safe models that generate and edit images, video, vectors, and audio, integrated across Creative Cloud and available as a web application and APIs with access to partner models.

resources.label: Adobe Firefly Creative Production
resources.description: Firefly's governed production workflow layer for enterprises — creative actions, orchestration, and integrations that automate repetitive production and generate consistent on-brand variations at scale.

resources.label: Adobe Firefly Custom Models
resources.description: Fine-tuned Firefly models trained on an organisation's own brand assets — styles, products, characters — that generate on-brand imagery usable in Firefly, Express, and GenStudio.

resources.label: Adobe Firefly Design Intelligence
resources.description: Firefly's enterprise design-system offering — design teams codify brand guidelines as trained StyleIDs that global creators then apply to produce design-compliant, contextually adapted assets.

resources.label: Adobe Firefly Foundry
resources.description: Adobe's managed service for building proprietary, IP-protected generative models deeply tuned on a business's own content across image, video, audio, vector, and 3D — the step beyond self-serve custom models.

resources.label: Adobe Firefly Services
resources.description: Enterprise APIs exposing Firefly and Creative Cloud automation for high-volume content production — generating variants, localising, and refreshing assets programmatically at scale.

resources.label: Firefly Video Model
resources.description: The video-generation model in the Firefly family — commercially safe text-to-video and image-to-video generation trained on licensed content.

resources.label: Adobe Fonts
resources.description: Adobe's font service — a library of licensed typefaces activated directly in Creative Cloud applications and on the web.

resources.label: Adobe Frame.io
resources.description: Adobe's cloud video review and collaboration platform — frame-accurate comments, version management, and camera-to-cloud uploads connecting production to post.

resources.label: Adobe Fresco
resources.description: The drawing and painting application for stylus and touch devices, with live watercolour and oil brushes that behave like physical media.

resources.label: Generate Podcast
resources.description: Acrobat's generative audio capability that converts document content into a two-host conversational podcast, with condensed and deep-dive script styles.

resources.label: Generative Expand
resources.description: Firefly-powered Photoshop feature that extends an image beyond its original borders, generating matching new content to fill the enlarged canvas.

resources.label: Generative Fill
resources.description: Firefly-powered Photoshop feature that generates new image content inside a selected region from a text prompt, matching the lighting and perspective of the surrounding image.

resources.label: Adobe GenStudio
resources.description: Adobe GenStudio: Umbrella generative AI content supply chain solution connecting Workfront, Firefly, AEM, and Content Analytics.

resources.label: Adobe GenStudio for Content Marketing
resources.description: The AI-first GenStudio application that applies the GenStudio creation-and-activation pipeline to content-marketing assets — briefs to on-brand marketing content — rather than to paid-media ads.

resources.label: Adobe GenStudio for Performance Marketing
resources.description: Adobe GenStudio for Performance Marketing: Native AI-first application for planning, creating, and optimizing campaign assets across paid media, email, and display ads.

resources.label: Adobe GenStudio Foundation
resources.description: The unified GenStudio interface that integrates data from the content-supply-chain applications — campaign plans, projects, assets, and performance — into one view with actionable insights across the chain.

resources.label: GenStudio Services
resources.description: The public REST API surface for GenStudio for Performance Marketing — retrieving approved experiences, listing and filtering experience summaries, and downloading assets with OAuth server-to-server authentication, so GenStudio content flows into external workflows and integrations.

resources.label: Headless CMS
resources.description: A content-management architecture that stores and serves content through APIs without prescribing the presentation layer, leaving rendering to any front end; in Adobe's portfolio, Experience Manager delivers headless content through Content Fragments and GraphQL.

resources.label: Adobe I/O
resources.description: Adobe's developer platform (now branded Adobe Developer) — the APIs, events, and runtime through which external code integrates with and extends Adobe products.

resources.label: Identity Graph
resources.description: The map of relationships between a person's identifiers — device IDs, email hashes, CRM IDs — that Adobe Experience Platform Identity Service maintains so fragmented records across channels resolve to one individual.

resources.label: Adobe Illustrator
resources.description: The professional vector graphics application — logos, icons, illustration, and type built from scalable paths rather than pixels.

resources.label: Adobe Illustrator (web)
resources.description: The browser edition of Illustrator — vector editing for lightweight and collaborative workflows.

resources.label: Adobe InCopy
resources.description: The editorial writing and copy-fitting application that lets writers work inside InDesign layouts in parallel with designers.

resources.label: Adobe InDesign
resources.description: The professional page layout and desktop publishing application for print and digital documents — books, magazines, brochures, and interactive PDFs.

resources.label: Journey Agent
resources.description: Journey-orchestration agent surfaced in AI Assistant within the Adobe Journey Optimizer Journeys workspace (B2C and B2B) — it builds journeys from natural-language prompts, analyses fallout, detects scheduling and audience conflicts with existing campaigns, and proposes adjustments before publication.

resources.label: Adobe Journey Optimizer
resources.description: Experience Platform's native journey application — orchestrating and delivering individual customer journeys, triggered messages, campaigns, and offers across email, mobile, and web from the Real-Time Customer Profile.

resources.label: Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
resources.description: The buying-group edition of Journey Optimizer — orchestrating account and buying-group journeys for B2B in coordination with Marketo Engage, and hosting the B2B agents including the Sales Qualifier add-on.

resources.label: Adobe Journey Optimizer Experimentation Accelerator
resources.description: Journey Optimizer's experimentation application — centralising past and active experiments, analysing results by audience, and accelerating the design of new tests; home of the Experimentation Agent.

resources.label: Journey Orchestration
resources.description: Coordinating each individual customer's next interaction across channels in response to their real-time behaviour and state, rather than broadcasting the same campaign to a whole segment; realised by Adobe Journey Optimizer.

resources.label: Lead Scoring
resources.description: Ranking prospects by fit and engagement signals so sales effort concentrates on the leads most likely to convert; a core Marketo Engage capability feeding sales-and-marketing alignment.

resources.label: Adobe Learning Manager
resources.description: Adobe's cloud learning management system for delivering and tracking training for customers, partners, and employees.

resources.label: Adobe Lightroom
resources.description: The cloud-centric photo editing and organisation application, syncing originals and edits across desktop, web, and mobile.

resources.label: Adobe Lightroom Classic
resources.description: The desktop-centric, file-based photo workflow application — local cataloguing, batch editing, and print output for photographers who keep originals on disk.

resources.label: Adobe Lightroom (web)
resources.description: The browser edition of Lightroom — viewing, culling, and editing synced photos from any machine.

resources.label: LLM Optimization Agent

resources.label: Adobe LLM Optimizer
resources.description: Adobe's generative-engine-optimisation product — a standalone application that improves how a brand's content is surfaced and cited by AI assistants and LLM-powered search, with an auto-identify, auto-suggest, auto-optimize workflow and dashboards for brand presence, agentic traffic, and LLM referral traffic.

resources.label: Marketing Automation
resources.description: The software category that automates repeatable marketing work — email sequences, lead nurturing, scoring, and campaign triggers — across the funnel; realised in Adobe's portfolio by Marketo Engage and Adobe Campaign.

resources.label: Adobe Marketo Engage
resources.description: Adobe's B2B marketing automation solution — lead management, nurturing, scoring, email marketing, and account-based marketing tied to CRM.

resources.label: Adobe Marketo Measure
resources.description: Adobe's B2B marketing attribution product (formerly Bizible) — multi-touch attribution and ROI measurement tied into CRM and the marketing platform.

resources.label: Adobe Media Encoder
resources.description: The batch transcoding and rendering companion that outputs Premiere Pro and After Effects work to delivery formats in the background.

resources.label: Adobe Mix Modeler
resources.description: Adobe's marketing measurement and planning application, combining media mix modelling with multi-touch attribution — measuring and optimising spend holistically across paid, earned, and owned channels using aggregate-level data.

resources.label: Mobile SDK
resources.description: The mobile-application counterpart to the Web SDK — it collects app events into the Edge Network and returns segment qualifications and personalised content in-session.

resources.label: Multivariate Testing

resources.label: Offer Decisioning

resources.label: Omnichannel Marketing
resources.description: The practice of coordinating consistent, connected customer messaging across every channel — email, web, mobile, paid media, in-person — as one continuous experience rather than running channels in isolation.

resources.label: Adobe PDF Services API
resources.description: Developer APIs for programmatic PDF operations — create, convert, OCR, extract, and manipulate documents inside applications and pipelines.

resources.label: PDF Spaces

resources.label: Personalization Engine
resources.description: A decisioning system that selects the content, offer, or experience each individual receives, using profile and behavioural data; realised in Adobe's portfolio by Adobe Target and Journey Optimizer decisioning.

resources.label: Adobe Photoshop
resources.description: The professional raster image editing and compositing application — layers, masking, retouching, and Firefly generative editing.

resources.label: Adobe Photoshop Express
resources.description: The lightweight mobile photo-editing application for quick corrections, filters, and social-ready output.

resources.label: Adobe Photoshop (web)
resources.description: The browser edition of Photoshop — editing PSDs and quick generative edits without a desktop install.

resources.label: Adobe Portfolio
resources.description: The website builder for personal creative portfolios, included with Creative Cloud membership.

resources.label: Predictive Analytics
resources.description: Using statistical and machine-learning models over historical data to forecast future customer behaviour — churn risk, conversion propensity, lifetime value — so action can be taken before the outcome occurs.

resources.label: Adobe Premiere (Mobile)
resources.description: The mobile Premiere application for editing and publishing video on phones and tablets, sharing the Premiere family's editing model in a touch-first form.

resources.label: Adobe Premiere Pro
resources.description: The professional non-linear video editing application — timeline editing, colour, audio, and delivery for film, broadcast, and online video.

resources.label: Product Advisor Agent
resources.description: Product-recommendation agent available in Adobe Brand Concierge — it advises end customers in real time, using unified profiles, behavioural data, and business rules to recommend the right products, plans, or offers, typically within a conversational interface.

resources.label: Adobe Product Analytics
resources.description: Experience Platform-based analytics application focused on product usage — user journeys, retention and cohort analysis, and funnels — for optimising digital product experience rather than marketing traffic.

resources.label: Product Support Agent

resources.label: Adobe Real-Time CDP
resources.description: Experience Platform's native customer data platform application — unifying known and pseudonymous data into actionable Real-Time Customer Profiles and activating audiences to destinations under governance controls.

resources.label: Adobe Real-Time CDP B2B Edition
resources.description: The B2B edition of Real-Time CDP — unifying person and account profiles, linking leads to accounts and opportunities for account-based segmentation and activation.

resources.label: Adobe Real-Time CDP Collaboration
resources.description: Real-Time CDP's data-collaboration application — two organisations discover audience overlap and measure campaign outcomes without exchanging their underlying customer databases.

resources.label: Real-Time Customer Profile
resources.description: Adobe Experience Platform's unified view of each customer — streaming and batch data from all connected sources merge into a single profile that updates in real time and powers segmentation, journeys, and personalisation.

resources.label: Reporting & Insights
resources.description: The Content Supply Chain phase in which content and campaign performance is measured and fed back into planning — served by Adobe Analytics, Customer Journey Analytics, and Content Analytics.

resources.label: Adobe Scan
resources.description: The mobile scanning application that captures paper documents as searchable, OCR-processed PDFs.

resources.label: Adobe Sensei
resources.description: Adobe's machine-intelligence framework powering AI features across Creative Cloud, Document Cloud, and Experience Cloud — auto-tagging, subject selection, personalisation scoring, anomaly detection — as embedded product intelligence rather than a standalone product.

resources.label: Sensei GenAI
resources.description: The generative AI services layer of Experience Cloud, built on large language models — it powers marketing copy generation, conversational assistance, and content variants inside applications such as Journey Optimizer and Experience Manager.

resources.label: Site Optimization Agent

resources.label: SPA
resources.description: Initialism for Single-Page Application — a web-application architecture in which one initial page load is updated dynamically by JavaScript instead of full page reloads; relevant to Adobe delivery because Experience Manager provides dedicated SPA authoring and rendering support.

resources.label: Adobe Stock
resources.description: Adobe's licensed stock-content marketplace — photos, video, vectors, templates, and 3D, searchable and licensable directly inside Creative Cloud applications.

resources.label: Adobe Substance 3D Designer
resources.description: The procedural material-authoring application in the Substance 3D family — node-based creation of tileable, parametric materials.

resources.label: Adobe Substance 3D Painter
resources.description: The 3D texture-painting application in the Substance 3D family — painting materials and details directly onto 3D models.

resources.label: Adobe Substance 3D Sampler
resources.description: The Substance 3D application for converting photographs and captures into usable 3D materials.

resources.label: Adobe Substance 3D Stager
resources.description: The Substance 3D scene staging and rendering application — assembling models, materials, lighting, and cameras into finished product shots.

resources.label: Success Studio

resources.label: Tags

resources.label: Adobe Target
resources.description: Adobe's testing and personalisation solution — A/B and multivariate testing plus rules-based and AI-driven personalisation of digital experiences.

resources.label: Web SDK

resources.label: Workflows, Planning & Metadata
resources.description: The Content Supply Chain phase covering campaign and work planning, workflow orchestration, and the metadata standards that keep content findable and traceable downstream — the phase Adobe Workfront serves.

resources.label: Adobe Workfront
resources.description: Adobe's enterprise work management platform connecting marketing strategy to execution — planning, project management, workflows, approvals, and resource management with real-time visibility.

resources.label: Adobe Workfront Planning
resources.description: Workfront's planning layer — connected workspaces that organise campaigns, budgets, and tasks into linked records for end-to-end marketing-operations visibility.

resources.label: Adobe Workfront Workflow
resources.description: Workfront's execution layer — projects, tasks, multi-stage reviews and approvals, and workflow automation across teams.

resources.label: Adobe XD
resources.description: The UI and UX design and prototyping application for screen experiences — artboards, components, and interactive prototypes.

resources.label: XDM
resources.description: Initialism for Experience Data Model — the open schema standard underpinning all Experience Platform data.

resources.label: Adult Professional Learner
resources.description: Adult professional with self-directed learning preferences.

resources.label: Agent Skill

resources.label: Agentic Instructional Pipeline

resources.label: UNESCO AI Competency Frameworks

resources.label: Ally

resources.label: Analogy
resources.description: Comparison to a familiar concept used to explain or validate a claim

resources.label: Analytic Rubric

resources.label: Analyze Verb
resources.description: Bloom's Level 4 action verbs indicating analysis-level learning objectives

resources.label: Anaphora
resources.description: Repetition of the same word or phrase at the start of successive clauses for emphasis

resources.label: Anaphora Marker
resources.description: Repeated word or phrase at the beginning of successive clauses

resources.label: Animation Only Carrier
resources.description: Essential information that can only be accessed via animation — inaccessible to static reading (anti-pattern)

resources.label: Animation Type
resources.description: Animation styles and motion graphics techniques used in learning content

resources.label: Antithesis
resources.description: Juxtaposition of contrasting ideas in parallel grammatical structure

resources.label: Apply Verb
resources.description: Bloom's Level 3 action verbs indicating application-level learning objectives

resources.label: Assessment For Learning
resources.description: Formative assessment (AfL) used diagnostically to tailor instruction and provide feedback during the learning process.

resources.description: Specific question or task formats used in assessments

resources.label: Assessment Of Learning

resources.label: Asynchronous Delivery Block

resources.label: Asynchronous Learning

resources.label: Attribution Marker
resources.description: Explicit attribution of a claim to a named source — enables argument provenance tracking

resources.label: Audience Analysis
resources.description: The discipline of researching an audience's knowledge, disposition and four-part needs — functional, emotional, social, aspirational — before communicating, using psychological profiling frameworks.

resources.label: Audience As Hero
resources.description: Narrative principle where the audience is the protagonist and the presenter is the mentor/guide.

resources.label: Audience Design
resources.description: The cognitive process by which speakers tailor speech to a listener's knowledge — common-ground models, egocentric referential error under load, and neural-alignment evidence.

resources.label: Audio Element
